# Glyphbound: code architecture

> Written by the architect (Claude Code) on 2026-11-12. Source of truth for how the C++ is organized.
> Design lives in `Design/GDD.md`; this file says how the code implements it. Keep it short and current.

## Principles
1. **Data, not code.** Every gameplay number lives in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` and is read through `UGBDataSubsystem`. Code never hardcodes damage, costs, speeds, durations, sizes or timings. The JSON ships as loose files, so numbers can be tuned in a packaged build with a text editor (`gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing).
2. **One stat system.** A number is a *named stat*: base value from data, then modifiers. `UGBStatsComponent` evaluates `(Base + adds) * multipliers` (or an override). Skill-tree nodes, armor, status effects, air passives and the weapon enchant are all just groups of modifiers with a source name. Nothing else changes numbers.
3. **One damage path.** Everything that hurts goes through `UGBCombatLibrary::DealDamage(Target, FGBDamageInfo)`. Shields, resistances, teams, on-hit effects and kill credit hook in there once.
4. **Spells are data + a behavior.** A spell is a `FGBSpellDefinition` (params with `Base/Min/Max/ScaledBy`) plus the class of an `AGBSpellActor` behavior. The QTE result (power, reach) scales the params tagged for it. A new spell that fits an existing behavior is a JSON entry, no code.
5. **Shared pieces.** One projectile (`AGBProjectile`) for staff bolts, spell projectiles, enemy shots and grenades. One status-effect component for slows, burns, potions and buffs. One interact interface for portals, chests, pickups and the seal.
6. **Text in git.** No binary assets are required to run: input actions, the test arena, placeholder shapes and placeholder pixel sprites are all built in C++ from text. `Content/` is ignored by git except `Content/Data/`.
7. **No GAS.** Unreal's Gameplay Ability System was considered and rejected for the jam: it needs a lot of boilerplate and asset setup, and the game's needs (costs, cooldowns, timed effects, stat upgrades) are covered by principles 2-4 in a few hundred lines we fully control.
8. **PIE is human-only.** Agents build, run the pure-logic tests and package; a person plays.

## Module layout (`Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound`, one runtime module, prefix `GB`)
Includes are relative to the module root: `#include "Stats/GBStatsComponent.h"`.

| Folder | What | Key types |
|---|---|---|
| `Core/` | Shared enums, stat names, placeholders (plain shapes and pixel-textured structures), game mode, dev commands | `GBTypes.h`, `GBStatNames.h`, `GBPlaceholder.h` (`SetupTexturedShape`), `AGBGameMode`, `UGBGameInstance`, `GBDevCommands.cpp` (`gb.Smoke`) |
| `Data/` | Definitions and the JSON loader | `GBDataTypes.h`, `UGBDataSubsystem` |
| `Stats/` | Stats + modifiers, health/mana | `UGBStatsComponent`, `UGBAttributeComponent` |
| `Combat/` | Damage (one path, one global `OnDamageDealt` event), status effects, projectile, explosion shockwave | `UGBCombatLibrary`, `UGBStatusEffectComponent`, `AGBProjectile`, `AGBExplosionEffect` |
| `Player/` | Character, controller, input | `AGBPlayerCharacter`, `AGBPlayerController`, `UGBInputSet` |
| `Weapons/` | Held items and slots | `UGBEquipmentComponent`, `AGBHeldItem`, `AGBStaff`, `AGBGun`, `AGBSword` |
| `Spells/` | Spellbook, cast resolution, behaviors | `UGBSpellbookComponent`, `FGBSpellCast`, `AGBSpellActor`, `AGBSpell_*` |
| `QTE/` | Quick-time event | `FGBQTESession`, `FGBGestureRecognizer`, `UGBQTEComponent` |
| `World/` | Eras, progress, interactables, test arena | `UGBEraSubsystem`, `UGBEraComponent`, `UGBProgressSubsystem`, `IGBInteractable`, `AGBPortal`, `AGBChest`, `AGBPickup`, `AGBCheckpointVolume`, `AGBTestArena` |
| `AI/` | Enemies (navmesh path, local steering fallback, stuck check) and encounters | `AGBEnemyCharacter`, `GBSteering` (pure decision, tested), `AGBEncounter` |
| `Items/` | Inventory, consumables, armor, recipes | `UGBInventoryComponent` |
| `Progression/` | Skill trees | `UGBSkillTreeComponent` |
| `UI/` | Canvas HUD (two skins), menus, pixel sprites | `AGBHUD`, `UGBPixelSpriteLibrary` |
| `Tests/` | Pure-logic automation tests | `Glyphbound.<Area>.<Name>` |

## Data files (`Glyphbound/Content/Data`)
`Player.json`, `QTE.json`, `Game.json`, `Spells.json`, `Weapons.json`, `StatusEffects.json`, `Items.json` (items + recipes), `Enemies.json`, `Encounters.json`, `Skills.json`, `Sprites.json`. Schemas are the structs in `Data/GBDataTypes.h` (field name = JSON key). Stat and parameter names are the constants in `Core/GBStatNames.h`.

Modifier keys: an actor stat (`MoveSpeed`), `Weapon.<Id>.<Stat>`, `Weapon.<Slot>.<Stat>` (`Weapon.Staff`, `Weapon.Gun`, `Weapon.Sword`), `Weapon.All.<Stat>`, `Spell.<Id>.<Param>`, `Spell.All.<Param>`, `QTE.TimeDilation`...

Standard status effect ids (defined in `StatusEffects.json`, referenced from other files): `Burn`, `Shock`, `Slow`, `Chill`, `HealthPotion`, `ManaPotion`, `HealthInjection`, `Enchant_Fire`, `Enchant_Lightning`, `Enchant_Ice`.

## How the main flows run
- **Cast:** input -> `UGBSpellbookComponent::TryCastSlot` (checks staff in hand, known, cooldown, mana; spends mana) -> `UGBQTEComponent::StartQTE` (slow time, sequence = power, gesture = reach; or instant when off) -> `GBSpell::ResolveCast` (data -> QTE scaling -> modifiers) -> spawn the behavior actor -> it deals damage through `UGBCombatLibrary`.
- **Shoot:** input -> `AGBGun` (fire interval, magazine, spread, recoil, pellets; every number via `GetStat`) -> hitscan -> headshot and distance falloff math in `UGBCombatLibrary` -> `DealDamage`.
- **Era travel:** `AGBPortal::Interact` -> `UGBEraSubsystem::RequestTravel` (fade out, swap era for `UGBEraComponent` actors and `_Past` / `_Future` sub-levels, teleport, restore health/mana/ammo, save checkpoint, fade in).
- **Progress:** encounters set flags in `UGBProgressSubsystem` when cleared; `UGBEraComponent` reads flags, which is how era-gated zones and past-to-future unlocks are built. Death restores the last checkpoint snapshot; flags are never rolled back (enemies do not respawn).
- **Upgrades:** `UGBSkillTreeComponent::Unlock` adds the node's modifiers to the player's stats; weapons and spells pick them up on their next read.

## Conventions
- Game text in English. Code comments in English. ASCII only in source files.
- Native multicast delegates (C++ project; no Blueprint graphs needed).
- No custom collision channels: projectiles and queries use the default channels and filter by team in code.
- Pointers to definitions are not kept across frames (data can be reloaded): keep the id, look it up.
- Tests: only pure logic that is easy to break and hard to see by playing; each one must be able to fail; names `Glyphbound.<Area>.<Name>` where a name is never also a prefix of another.
- Build: `powershell -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1` (Editor closed). One build at a time per machine.
- Art rule in code: characters, items and effects are camera-facing pixel sprites; **structures are 3D shapes with pixel tiles** (`GBPlaceholder::SetupTexturedShape`, tiles are sprites of `Sprites.json` named `tile_*`). The material behind it (`M_PixelSurface`) is the only binary asset and is generated by `Tools/Jam/Make-Materials.ps1`, never edited by hand.
- A structure that looks different in each era has ONE hidden collision body present in both eras and two non-colliding looks (PastOnly / FutureOnly), so footing and navigation never change on era travel.
- UI that reacts to combat listens to `UGBCombatLibrary::OnDamageDealt()`; nothing in combat code knows about the HUD.

411:- **Sustained spells (flamethrower), changed by the owner (2026-11-12):** after the QTE the flamethrower runs **while its spell key is held**, until the key is released or the mana runs out (also on weapon switch or death). No time limit. Provisional (architect): it pays a smaller cost at the start (10 mana, always spent, like every QTE spell) and then drains 15 mana per second; if the key was already released when the QTE ends, it still burns for a short minimum (0.75 s) so the cast is never wasted; the cooldown starts at the cast. All values in `Spells.json` (`ManaCost`, `ManaPerSecond`, `MinDuration`).
414:- **New spell perks (owner's list, placement by the architect):** in the spell tree, each under its element's column (fire, lightning, ice), with no prerequisite so they can be tested right away. Deep Freeze: the ice floor slows by 50% at normal QTE power (the slow effect, `StatusEffects.json`), so +5 points per rank makes 55 / 60 / 65%; the cap is **80%** (also reached by a perfect QTE with 3 ranks). The cap is a general rule: any spell parameter can declare a `Cap` in `Spells.json`, applied after QTE scaling and perks.
416:- **Modifier keys by weapon type:** besides one weapon (`Weapon.Pistol.Damage`) and all weapons (`Weapon.All.Damage`), a modifier can target a slot: `Weapon.Gun.*`, `Weapon.Staff.*`, `Weapon.Sword.*`. The enchant uses `Weapon.Gun.Damage`, so it never buffs the staff or the sword.
421:- **Weapon enchant QTE:** part 1 scales how long the buff lasts; part 2 scales how strong it is. Only one enchant at a time. The enchanted gun deals the element's damage type and applies its effect on hit (fire burns, lightning shocks, ice chills).
422:- **Spell walls:** the fire wall does not block; it burns enemies that touch it. The ice wall blocks movement and shots and has health; anyone's shots can break it, the player's included. Enemies do not attack walls on purpose yet.
438:- **Head / weak point bonus per weapon** (owner, 2026-11-12): pistol x2; shotgun, rifle, staffs and sword x1.5. **Perks can raise it**: the weapon tree node "Marksman" adds +0.25 per rank (3 ranks) to every weapon, staff and sword included (provisional numbers). Spell projectiles get no head bonus unless a spell defines one.
439:- **Fireball shockwave:** pushes enemies away from the blast (strength scaled by QTE power).
442:- **Staff:** Apprentice staff 12 damage every 0.35 s, no mana cost. Ember staff 22 fire damage every 0.6 s and burns.
444:- **Enemies:** past orc 60 health, melee 12; future orc 70 health, ranged 9; brute (sub-boss placeholder) 320 health, melee 28.
445:- **Status effects:** burn 32 damage over 4 s; slow 50% for 4 s; chill 30% for 3 s; shock 40% for 1.5 s; health potion 60 over 10 s; injection 35 at once; enchant +25% gun damage for 20 s.

No time limit. Provisional (architect): it pays a smaller cost at the start (10 mana, always spent, like every QTE spell) and then drains 15 mana per second; if the key was already released when the QTE ends, it still burns for a short minimum (0.75 s) so the cast is never wasted; the cooldown starts at the cast. All values in `Spells.json` (`ManaCost`, `ManaPerSecond`, `MinDuration`).

Deep Freeze: the ice floor slows by 50% at normal QTE power (the slow effect, `StatusEffects.json`), so +5 points per rank makes 55 / 60 / 65%; the cap is **80%** (also reached by a perfect QTE with 3 ranks). content.text:
Ya revisé el código. Antes de preguntar, esto es lo que encontré, porque explica las preguntas:

**Lo que ya existe y se reutiliza (sin cambios de fondo)**
- Todo el daño pasa por una sola función, `UGBCombatLibrary::DealDamage` ([GBCombatLibrary.cpp](Source/Glyphbound/Combat/GBCombatLibrary.cpp)). Ahí se engancha la acumulación, de modo que cada impacto real se aplica una sola vez, venga de explosiones, proyectiles que atraviesan o ticks.
- Los efectos con tiempo los gestiona `UGBStatusEffectComponent`, y cada enemigo ya tiene el suyo. Ignite, Shock y Frost serán efectos de ese mismo sistema, definidos en `StatusEffects.json`.
- La regla de cabeza / punto débil ya existe en un solo sitio (`ApplyWeakPointBonus`), y la bonificación de acumulación sale de ahí.
- El lanzallamas (ticks de 0,3 s), las trampas (radio de detección distinto del de explosión, más Expanded Sigil) y el Ice Floor (ticks de 0,5 s, Deep Freeze, tope del 80 %) ya trabajan por intervalos. La acumulación va en esos mismos ticks.

**Conflictos con la especificación**
1. **Hoy cada golpe elemental ya aplica un efecto pequeño:**
   - **Fuego:** Fireball, Fire Wall, el lanzallamas, el bastón Ember y el encantamiento de fuego aplican *Burn* (32 de daño en 4 s).
   - **Rayo:** Lightning Bolt, Lightning Rune, Static Orb y el encantamiento de rayo aplican un efecto que **ya se llama "Shock"**: ralentiza un 40 % durante 1,5 s.
   - **Hielo:** el encantamiento de hielo aplica *Chill* (30 % de ralentización), y el Ice Floor aplica *Slow*.

   Si añado Ignite encima sin más, habría dos DOT. Y "Shock" quedaría con dos significados distintos.
2. **Las ralentizaciones hoy se multiplican:** un 50 % del Ice Floor y un 30 % de Chill dan un 65 %. La especificación pide que Frost no se sume sin control. Lo resuelvo con la regla de "gana la ralentización más fuerte", con su tope.
3. **No hay resistencias elementales:** hoy solo existe un `DamageTaken` general. Las resistencias al daño y a la acumulación por enemigo serán nuevas.
4. **El "Weapon Enchant" de este juego solo funciona con pistolas** (GDD). La espada elemental (gema) y el bastón Ember tienen elemento propio, pero no son "armas encantadas".

Las decisiones técnicas (cómo se interrumpe la carga de ataque, una sola acumulación por disparo de escopeta aunque acierten 8 perdigones, limpieza al morir, tests) las tomo yo. Me quedan dos preguntas de diseño:

questions.question: Hoy cada golpe elemental ya aplica un efecto pequeño: fuego = Burn (DOT corto), rayo = ralentización del 40% (que ya se llama "Shock"), encantamiento de hielo = Chill (ralentización del 30%). Con el nuevo sistema de acumulación (Ignite / Shock / Frost al llenar la barra), ¿qué hacemos con esos efectos por golpe?

options.label: Mantener Burn, quitar el resto (Recomendado)
options.description: Fuego conserva su Burn por golpe (Fireball sigue quemando como hoy), pero mientras Ignite esté activo no se aplica Burn: nunca hay dos DOT. Se quita la ralentización por golpe del rayo y el Chill del encantamiento de hielo, así cada elemento tiene una identidad clara. Ice Floor conserva su ralentización de zona.

options.label: Mantener todos
options.description: Los tres efectos por golpe siguen como hoy. El efecto de rayo por golpe se renombra a "Jolt" para liberar el nombre Shock. Ignite reemplaza a Burn mientras dura. Las ralentizaciones no se multiplican: gana la más fuerte.

options.label: Quitar todos
options.description: El único efecto elemental es el estado que se activa al llenar la barra. Fireball deja de quemar en cada golpe (solo quema al activar Ignite). Ice Floor conserva su ralentización de zona.

content.content:
# Game Design Document (working draft)

> Epic AI MegaJam 2026 · Theme: **DIRECTOR'S CUT** · Unreal Engine 5.9.0
> Status: **v0.21, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus eleven rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.
> Audience: **the architect** = whichever Claude Code chat is currently implementing the game. There is normally only one at a time, and it is replaced when its context fills up or its tasks are done. This document is the source of truth that every new architect chat reads first. Implementation is delegated as `CLAUDE.md` says ("Implementador").
> Project code name: **Glyphbound** (provisional; the game title is still TBD). Written in English because it is part of the public dev log (Glass Box) and the jam requires English.

## Changelog
- v0.21 (2026-11-12): owner: a strong hit (30% of health or more) interrupts the flamethrower, with a camera shake; the spell description says "a strong hit" without the number.
- v0.20 (2026-11-12): owner: six new spell-tree perks (one per spell that had none); the flamethrower runs while its key is held, until the key is released or the mana runs out.
- v0.19 (2026-11-12): owner: when ground spells overlap, the one placed last covers the others completely, and they never flicker.
- v0.18 (2026-11-12): owner asked for a "+1 skill point" button on the skill tree screen, to test perks.
- v0.17 (2026-11-12): owner, after playing: the pixel-art figure of the lightning rune and the ice floor must cover the whole area of the spell, lying on the ground, not a small sprite in the middle.
- v0.16 (2026-11-12): owner asked for a way to reset the perks from the skill tree screen, to test them better. All spent skill points come back.
## 6. Magic (4 elements + weapon enchant)
Each element has 3 entries. Air is passives only; the other three are active spells.

| Element | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fire** | Fireball (projectile; **always explodes with a shockwave**, on an enemy, on the world or at the end of its range) | Fire wall | Flamethrower (sustained DPS; **runs while the spell key is held**, until it is released or the mana runs out; **a strong hit interrupts it**) |
| **Lightning** | Lightning bolt (projectile) | Lightning rune trap on the ground; triggers when an enemy walks over it | Static-electricity ball: moves and damages every enemy around it |
| **Ice** | Ice shield (**summoned by the spell, then raised by holding the Block key**, like the shield of a first-person RPG; it only protects while raised; cooldown and limits) | Ice wall | Ice floor: slows enemies, light crowd control |
| **Air** (passives) | Double jump | Improved dash | Increased movement speed |

### Spell loadout
- The player has **5 spells equipped** at a time and can **equip and unequip** them freely.
- **Air passives are always active**: they are not equipped and do not take a slot.
- **Starting spells:** Fireball (very early tier), Lightning bolt (early tier), Ice wall.

### Learning the other spells: elemental zones
- The **medieval castle** has **elemental zones**, one per element.
- Each zone has a **challenge**: a wave, a sub-boss or a boss.
- After the challenge the player gets the element's **knowledge** (from a chest, a book or similar) and **unlocks the missing spells of that element** (fire: fire wall + flamethrower; lightning: rune trap + static ball; ice: ice shield + ice floor).
- **Air passives** are learned the same way, in the air zone.
- The spell tree then upgrades what the player knows.
- **Spells can only be cast with the staff in hand.** With a gun in hand, the only spell available is the weapon enchant. To cast, the player switches to the staff mid-fight.
- Keys: see §9.

### Ice shield (owner, 2026-11-12)
- Casting it (with its QTE) **summons** the shield for a time. It is not a force field in front of the player.
- The player **raises it by holding a secondary key** (Block) and lowers it by letting go. It protects from the front **only while raised**.
- Provisional details (architect): Block is **Q** on keyboard and **L2** on gamepad; it needs the staff or the sword in hand (with a gun, L2 is aim); while raised the player moves slower and cannot attack or cast; the shield has health and breaks when it runs out; other spells can be cast while it is summoned and lowered.

### Weapon enchant (always equipped)
- A spell that **cannot be unequipped**.
- **Only usable with a gun in hand** (it enchants the gun).
- Animation: the **left hand draws a magic glyph over the weapon held in the right hand**.
- Effect: the weapon is **temporarily buffed with magic** of one element.
- **Element:** chosen by the player when equipping the spell.
- **Uses the QTE** like every other spell (§7).
- **Does not work on the elemental sword.**
- Duration, cost and exact buff per element: **TBD**.

### General
- Spells cost **mana**.
- **Health and mana regenerate on their own** (potions and the injection speed it up). **No stamina.**
- Numbers for each spell (damage, cost, cooldowns, upgrade tiers): **TBD**, given later.
- The ice shield's exact limits (duration, damage absorbed, break behavior): **TBD**.

## 7. Spell-casting quick-time event
**Status:** wanted for every spell, the enchant included; still a trial for the 4-day schedule, so it must be possible to switch it off (spells then cast at a fixed default strength).

Purpose: make magic feel more elaborate than pulling a trigger.

### Flow
1. Player casts. **Time slows** by about **90%** (world at ~10% speed). Inspired by the slowed time some games use while the player picks combat hacks.
2. **Part 1 — button sequence → POWER.** Random sequence.
   - Keyboard & mouse: movement keys (W, A, S, D).
   - Gamepad: the four face buttons (A/B/X/Y or Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle).
3. **Part 2 — gesture → REACH.**
   - Mouse: left-to-right, top-to-bottom, a circle, etc.
   - Gamepad: the right stick.
4. Spell fires with its parameters scaled by the two results; time returns to normal.

### Grading and cost
- Each step counts on its own: every mistake lowers the result of its part.
- **The spell is cast if the player gets at least one step right.** It fails only if **every** step is missed.
- **Mana is always spent**, even when the spell fails.

### What each part scales
| Spell | Part 1 (power) | Part 2 (reach) |
- Game and team name.

## 18. Provisional rules and numbers picked by the architect (2026-11-12)
The owner asked the architect not to stop for missing design details. Everything below was chosen so the prototype could be built; **all of it is provisional** and waits for the owner's word. Numbers are in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` and can be changed there without touching code.

### Rules
- **Jumps commit to their direction (owner, 2026-11-12):** like a real jump, the direction cannot be changed in the air (air control 0; the same when walking off a ledge). The direction is chosen at takeoff: the movement keys held at that moment. The second jump can choose a new direction and then commits again. Provisional details (architect): a jump from standing with a direction held leaves at 60% of walking speed at least; the second jump with a direction held leaves at walking speed at least, and with no direction held it keeps the current drift. The dash still works in the air and is not affected.
- **Double jump on day 1:** the player starts knowing the air passive "Double jump" so it can be tested now. In the real game it is learned in the air zone (§6); remove it from `Player.json` `StartingSpells` then.
- **Dash:** available from the start (the air passive only improves it). It goes in the movement direction (forward when standing still), works in the air, gives no invulnerability, and does not refill jumps.
- **Owning weapons:** decided by the owner for staffs (section 8): picked-up weapons go to the inventory and are equipped by hand. Provisional part: guns and the sword follow the same rule; each owned gun keeps its own ammo while stored.
- **Reload:** the bullets left in the old magazine are lost (classic tactical style). A gun reloads by itself when its magazine runs dry. Ammo pickups give one spare magazine, up to the gun's maximum.
- **Sustained spells (flamethrower), changed by the owner (2026-11-12):** after the QTE the flamethrower runs **while its spell key is held**, until the key is released or the mana runs out (also on weapon switch or death). No time limit. Provisional (architect): it pays a smaller cost at the start (10 mana, always spent, like every QTE spell) and then drains 15 mana per second; if the key was already released when the QTE ends, it still burns for a short minimum (0.75 s) so the cast is never wasted; the cooldown starts at the cast. All values in `Spells.json` (`ManaCost`, `ManaPerSecond`, `MinDuration`).
- **Strong hit interrupts the flamethrower (owner, 2026-11-12):** a single hit that takes **30% or more of the player's maximum health** stops it at once, and the camera shakes. The in-game description says "a strong hit", never the number. Provisional (architect): measured against maximum health (not current health), on the damage actually taken after the ice shield and armor; the threshold is a spell parameter (`InterruptHitFraction`, so any sustained spell can use it); the shake is short (about 0.35 s, a few degrees, values in `Game.json`), only moves the view, never the aim; the mana already spent is not refunded and the cooldown is unchanged.
- **Flamethrower damage ticks (owner, 2026-11-12):** damage is dealt in fixed time steps, never per frame, so it does not depend on the frame rate: one tick every **0.3 s** (`TickInterval`), each dealing `DamagePerSecond x 0.3` (the mana drain follows the same ticks). If a frame is longer than a tick, the missed ticks still happen.
- **New spell perks (owner's list, placement by the architect):** in the spell tree, each under its element's column (fire, lightning, ice), with no prerequisite so they can be tested right away. Deep Freeze: the ice floor slows by 50% at normal QTE power (the slow effect, `StatusEffects.json`), so +5 points per rank makes 55 / 60 / 65%; the cap is **80%** (also reached by a perfect QTE with 3 ranks). The cap is a general rule: any spell parameter can declare a `Cap` in `Spells.json`, applied after QTE scaling and perks.
- **Ice shield QTE:** part 1 (power) scales its duration and health; part 2 (reach) scales how much frontal damage it blocks.
- **Modifier keys by weapon type:** besides one weapon (`Weapon.Pistol.Damage`) and all weapons (`Weapon.All.Damage`), a modifier can target a slot: `Weapon.Gun.*`, `Weapon.Staff.*`, `Weapon.Sword.*`. The enchant uses `Weapon.Gun.Damage`, so it never buffs the staff or the sword.
- **Explosions and enemy melee need a clear line** to their target: no damage through walls or through the ice wall.
- **Enemies and cover (after the first play-test):** enemies walk around obstacles. A melee enemy only starts its attack when it sees the player; a ranged enemy that loses sight stops aiming and moves until it sees the player again. Enemies do not walk off ledges on their own; one that falls out of the map dies without drops.
- **Projectile explosions push enemies back** (knockback is a spell parameter, scaled by QTE power); they do not push the player.
- **Falling:** the kill height is 2,500 cm below the floor of the level (`Game.json` `KillZ`).
- **Weapon enchant QTE:** part 1 scales how long the buff lasts; part 2 scales how strong it is. Only one enchant at a time. The enchanted gun deals the element's damage type and applies its effect on hit (fire burns, lightning shocks, ice chills).
- **Spell walls:** the fire wall does not block; it burns enemies that touch it. The ice wall blocks movement and shots and has health; anyone's shots can break it, the player's included. Enemies do not attack walls on purpose yet.
- **QTE:** a wrong key consumes its step. A gesture is judged when the hand stops for a moment or the stroke is clearly complete. If both parts are fully missed the spell fizzles, and the mana is still spent and the cooldown still starts.
- **New spells** go to the first free loadout slot.
- **Ground spell figures (architect, after the owner's note):** the figure is the spell's sprite stretched to the diameter of its area, a few cm above the floor, keeping the pixels sharp; transparent pixels show the floor. It does not turn with the camera; it keeps the yaw the player was facing when casting. The rune shows dimmer until it is armed. The old colored disc is gone.
- **Overlapping ground spells (owner, 2026-11-12):** the figure placed last is drawn on top of every figure it overlaps, completely (an ice floor cast over a rune hides the rune where they overlap; a rune cast over an ice floor shows over it), and overlapping figures never flicker. Provisional (architect): each new figure sits a little higher than the highest figure it overlaps (1.5 cm per layer, values in `Game.json`); this is only how it looks, the spells' areas and effects do not change.
- **Skill reset (owner asked for it, details provisional):** a "Reset skills" button on the skill tree screen (K, and the Skills page of the inventory), also the R key (Y / Triangle on a gamepad) while that screen is open. Free, any time, no confirmation, refunds exactly the points that were spent (even if a node's cost changed in `Skills.json` since). Whether the final game keeps it free, limits it (for example only at portals) or keeps it only as a test option is open.
- **"+1 skill point" button (owner asked for it, to test perks):** on the same screen, left of the skill points; each click adds one free point to the pool (no key, no limit). A reset refunds only what was paid, so free points stay. It is a test option: it must be removed or hidden before the jam submission (provisional, architect).
- **Elemental sword:** the hilt and the gems are not consumed when forging, so the player re-forges from the inventory to switch element.
- **Enemies:** once hit, an enemy chases the player from any distance. Enemies of the other era are frozen and hidden, not simulated.
- **Encounters:** if the player dies during one, its living enemies are removed and it starts again from wave 1 on return. Progress flags are never rolled back.
- **Checkpoints:** saved at the start, on every era travel, on entering a checkpoint zone and when an encounter is cleared. Death sends the player back to the checkpoint's place and era with full health, mana and ammo, and **keeps everything collected since** (items, weapons, spells, skill points): pickups and chests do not come back, so rolling the inventory back would lose rewards for good (found by the code review).
- **Consumables** can be used at full health or mana (they are wasted).
- **Art rule on pickups:** cyberpunk items (injection, grenade, magazine, sword hilt) lie on the floor as 3D shapes; medieval ones (potions, gems, books, staffs) as pixel-art sprites.

### Numbers (first pass, all in the JSON files)
- **Jumps:** each jump rises about 2 m (was 1.2 m); the double jump adds a second one of the same height.
- **Head / weak point bonus per weapon** (owner, 2026-11-12): pistol x2; shotgun, rifle, staffs and sword x1.5. **Perks can raise it**: the weapon tree node "Marksman" adds +0.25 per rank (3 ranks) to every weapon, staff and sword included (provisional numbers). Spell projectiles get no head bonus unless a spell defines one.
- **Fireball shockwave:** pushes enemies away from the blast (strength scaled by QTE power).
- **Player:** 100 health (regenerates 2/s after 5 s without damage), 100 mana (6/s after 1.5 s), speed 750, dash 7 m in 0.18 s every 1.2 s.
- **QTE:** 4 keys, 1 gesture, 4 s in real time (raised from 3 s by the owner), world at 10% speed.
- **Staff:** Apprentice staff 12 damage every 0.35 s, no mana cost. Ember staff 22 fire damage every 0.6 s and burns.
- **Guns:** pistol 18 damage, 12 rounds, 4 spare magazines; shotgun 8 pellets of 10, 6 rounds, strong up close; rifle automatic, 14 damage, 30 rounds, stronger far away. Headshots: pistol x2, shotgun and rifle x1.5.
- **Enemies:** past orc 60 health, melee 12; future orc 70 health, ranged 9; brute (sub-boss placeholder) 320 health, melee 28.
- **Status effects:** burn 32 damage over 4 s; slow 50% for 4 s; chill 30% for 3 s; shock 40% for 1.5 s; health potion 60 over 10 s; injection 35 at once; enchant +25% gun damage for 20 s.
- **Skill trees:** 6 nodes each, 1-2 points per rank, up to 3 ranks.
- Every spell number in `Spells.json`.

| **Fire** | Fireball (projectile; **always explodes with a shockwave**, on an enemy, on the world or at the end of its range) | Fire wall | Flamethrower (sustained DPS; **runs while the spell key is held**, until it is released or the mana runs out; **a strong hit interrupts it**) |
| **Lightning** | Lightning bolt (projectile) | Lightning rune trap on the ground; triggers when an enemy walks over it | Static-electricity ball: moves and damages every enemy around it |
| **Ice** | Ice shield (**summoned by the spell, then raised by holding the Block key**, like the shield of a first-person RPG; it only protects while raised; cooldown and limits) | Ice wall | Ice floor: slows enemies, light crowd control |
| **Air** (passives) | Double jump | Improved dash | Increased movement speed |

### Spell loadout
- The player has **5 spells equipped** at a time and can **equip and unequip** them freely.
- **Air passives are always active**: they are not equipped and do not take a slot.
- **Starting spells:** Fireball (very early tier), Lightning bolt (early tier), Ice wall.

### Learning the other spells: elemental zones
- The **medieval castle** has **elemental zones**, one per element.
- Each zone has a **challenge**: a wave, a sub-boss or a boss.
- After the challenge the player gets the element's **knowledge** (from a chest, a book or similar) and **unlocks the missing spells of that element** (fire: fire wall + flamethrower; lightning: rune trap + static ball; ice: ice shield + ice floor).
- **Air passives** are learned the same way, in the air zone.
- The spell tree then upgrades what the player knows.
- **Spells can only be cast with the staff in hand.** With a gun in hand, the only spell available is the weapon enchant. To cast, the player switches to the staff mid-fight.
- Keys: see §9.

### Ice shield (owner, 2026-11-12)
- Casting it (with its QTE) **summons** the shield for a time. It is not a force field in front of the player.
- The player **raises it by holding a secondary key** (Block) and lowers it by letting go. It protects from the front **only while raised**.
- Provisional details (architect): Block is **Q** on keyboard and **L2** on gamepad; it needs the staff or the sword in hand (with a gun, L2 is aim); while raised the player moves slower and cannot attack or cast; the shield has health and breaks when it runs out; other spells can be cast while it is summoned and lowered.

### Weapon enchant (always equipped)
- A spell that **cannot be unequipped**.
- **Only usable with a gun in hand** (it enchants the gun).
- Animation: the **left hand draws a magic glyph over the weapon held in the right hand**.
- Effect: the weapon is **temporarily buffed with magic** of one element.
- **Element:** chosen by the player when equipping the spell.
- **Uses the QTE** like every other spell (§7).
- **Does not work on the elemental sword.**
- Duration, cost and exact buff per element: **TBD**.

### General
- Spells cost **mana**.
- **Health and mana regenerate on their own** (potions and the injection speed it up). **No stamina.**
- Numbers for each spell (damage, cost, cooldowns, upgrade tiers): **TBD**, given later.
- The ice shield's exact limits (duration, damage absorbed, break behavior): **TBD**.

## 7. Spell-casting quick-time event
**Status:** wanted for every spell, the enchant included; still a trial for the 4-day schedule, so it must be possible to switch it off (spells then cast at a fixed default strength).

Purpose: make magic feel more elaborate than pulling a trigger.

### Flow
1. Player casts. **Time slows** by about **90%** (world at ~10% speed). Inspired by the slowed time some games use while the player picks combat hacks.
2. **Part 1 — button sequence → POWER.** Random sequence.
   - Keyboard & mouse: movement keys (W, A, S, D).
   - Gamepad: the four face buttons (A/B/X/Y or Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle).
3. **Part 2 — gesture → REACH.**
   - Mouse: left-to-right, top-to-bottom, a circle, etc.
   - Gamepad: the right stick.
4. Spell fires with its parameters scaled by the two results; time returns to normal.

### Grading and cost
- Each step counts on its own: every mistake lowers the result of its part.
- **The spell is cast if the player gets at least one step right.** It fails only if **every** step is missed.
- **Mana is always spent**, even when the spell fails.

### What each part scales
| Spell | Part 1 (power) | Part 2 (reach) |
- Game and team name.

## 18. Provisional rules and numbers picked by the architect (2026-11-12)
The owner asked the architect not to stop for missing design details. Everything below was chosen so the prototype could be built; **all of it is provisional** and waits for the owner's word. Numbers are in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json` and can be changed there without touching code.

### Rules
- **Jumps commit to their direction (owner, 2026-11-12):** like a real jump, the direction cannot be changed in the air (air control 0; the same when walking off a ledge). The direction is chosen at takeoff: the movement keys held at that moment. The second jump can choose a new direction and then commits again. Provisional details (architect): a jump from standing with a direction held leaves at 60% of walking speed at least; the second jump with a direction held leaves at walking speed at least, and with no direction held it keeps the current drift. The dash still works in the air and is not affected.
- **Double jump on day 1:** the player starts knowing the air passive "Double jump" so it can be tested now. In the real game it is learned in the air zone (§6); remove it from `Player.json` `StartingSpells` then.
- **Dash:** available from the start (the air passive only improves it). It goes in the movement direction (forward when standing still), works in the air, gives no invulnerability, and does not refill jumps.
- **Owning weapons:** decided by the owner for staffs (section 8): picked-up weapons go to the inventory and are equipped by hand. Provisional part: guns and the sword follow the same rule; each owned gun keeps its own ammo while stored.
- **Reload:** the bullets left in the old magazine are lost (classic tactical style). A gun reloads by itself when its magazine runs dry. Ammo pickups give one spare magazine, up to the gun's maximum.
- **Sustained spells (flamethrower), changed by the owner (2026-11-12):** after the QTE the flamethrower runs **while its spell key is held**, until the key is released or the mana runs out (also on weapon switch or death). No time limit. Provisional (architect): it pays a smaller cost at the start (10 mana, always spent, like every QTE spell) and then drains 15 mana per second; if the key was already released when the QTE ends, it still burns for a short minimum (0.75 s) so the cast is never wasted; the cooldown starts at the cast. All values in `Spells.json` (`ManaCost`, `ManaPerSecond`, `MinDuration`).
- **Strong hit interrupts the flamethrower (owner, 2026-11-12):** a single hit that takes **30% or more of the player's maximum health** stops it at once, and the camera shakes. The in-game description says "a strong hit", never the number. Provisional (architect): measured against maximum health (not current health), on the damage actually taken after the ice shield and armor; the threshold is a spell parameter (`InterruptHitFraction`, so any sustained spell can use it); the shake is short (about 0.35 s, a few degrees, values in `Game.json`), only moves the view, never the aim; the mana already spent is not refunded and the cooldown is unchanged.
- **Flamethrower damage ticks (owner, 2026-11-12):** damage is dealt in fixed time steps, never per frame, so it does not depend on the frame rate: one tick every **0.3 s** (`TickInterval`), each dealing `DamagePerSecond x 0.3` (the mana drain follows the same ticks). If a frame is longer than a tick, the missed ticks still happen.
- **New spell perks (owner's list, placement by the architect):** in the spell tree, each under its element's column (fire, lightning, ice), with no prerequisite so they can be tested right away. Deep Freeze: the ice floor slows by 50% at normal QTE power (the slow effect, `StatusEffects.json`), so +5 points per rank makes 55 / 60 / 65%; the cap is **80%** (also reached by a perfect QTE with 3 ranks). The cap is a general rule: any spell parameter can declare a `Cap` in `Spells.json`, applied after QTE scaling and perks.
- **Ice shield QTE:** part 1 (power) scales its duration and health; part 2 (reach) scales how much frontal damage it blocks.
- **Modifier keys by weapon type:** besides one weapon (`Weapon.Pistol.Damage`) and all weapons (`Weapon.All.Damage`), a modifier can target a slot: `Weapon.Gun.*`, `Weapon.Staff.*`, `Weapon.Sword.*`. The enchant uses `Weapon.Gun.Damage`, so it never buffs the staff or the sword.
- **Explosions and enemy melee need a clear line** to their target: no damage through walls or through the ice wall.
- **Enemies and cover (after the first play-test):** enemies walk around obstacles. A melee enemy only starts its attack when it sees the player; a ranged enemy that loses sight stops aiming and moves until it sees the player again. Enemies do not walk off ledges on their own; one that falls out of the map dies without drops.
- **Projectile explosions push enemies back** (knockback is a spell parameter, scaled by QTE power); they do not push the player.
- **Falling:** the kill height is 2,500 cm below the floor of the level (`Game.json` `KillZ`).
- **Weapon enchant QTE:** part 1 scales how long the buff lasts; part 2 scales how strong it is. Only one enchant at a time. The enchanted gun deals the element's damage type and applies its effect on hit (fire burns, lightning shocks, ice chills).
- **Spell walls:** the fire wall does not block; it burns enemies that touch it. The ice wall blocks movement and shots and has health; anyone's shots can break it, the player's included. Enemies do not attack walls on purpose yet.
- **QTE:** a wrong key consumes its step. A gesture is judged when the hand stops for a moment or the stroke is clearly complete. If both parts are fully missed the spell fizzles, and the mana is still spent and the cooldown still starts.
- **New spells** go to the first free loadout slot.
- **Ground spell figures (architect, after the owner's note):** the figure is the spell's sprite stretched to the diameter of its area, a few cm above the floor, keeping the pixels sharp; transparent pixels show the floor. It does not turn with the camera; it keeps the yaw the player was facing when casting. The rune shows dimmer until it is armed. The old colored disc is gone.
- **Overlapping ground spells (owner, 2026-11-12):** the figure placed last is drawn on top of every figure it overlaps, completely (an ice floor cast over a rune hides the rune where they overlap; a rune cast over an ice floor shows over it), and overlapping figures never flicker. Provisional (architect): each new figure sits a little higher than the highest figure it overlaps (1.5 cm per layer, values in `Game.json`); this is only how it looks, the spells' areas and effects do not change.
- **Skill reset (owner asked for it, details provisional):** a "Reset skills" button on the skill tree screen (K, and the Skills page of the inventory), also the R key (Y / Triangle on a gamepad) while that screen is open. Free, any time, no confirmation, refunds exactly the points that were spent (even if a node's cost changed in `Skills.json` since). Whether the final game keeps it free, limits it (for example only at portals) or keeps it only as a test option is open.
- **"+1 skill point" button (owner asked for it, to test perks):** on the same screen, left of the skill points; each click adds one free point to the pool (no key, no limit). A reset refunds only what was paid, so free points stay. It is a test option: it must be removed or hidden before the jam submission (provisional, architect).
- **Elemental sword:** the hilt and the gems are not consumed when forging, so the player re-forges from the inventory to switch element.
- **Enemies:** once hit, an enemy chases the player from any distance. Enemies of the other era are frozen and hidden, not simulated.
- **Encounters:** if the player dies during one, its living enemies are removed and it starts again from wave 1 on return. Progress flags are never rolled back.
- **Checkpoints:** saved at the start, on every era travel, on entering a checkpoint zone and when an encounter is cleared. Death sends the player back to the checkpoint's place and era with full health, mana and ammo, and **keeps everything collected since** (items, weapons, spells, skill points): pickups and chests do not come back, so rolling the inventory back would lose rewards for good (found by the code review).
- **Consumables** can be used at full health or mana (they are wasted).
- **Art rule on pickups:** cyberpunk items (injection, grenade, magazine, sword hilt) lie on the floor as 3D shapes; medieval ones (potions, gems, books, staffs) as pixel-art sprites.

### Numbers (first pass, all in the JSON files)
- **Jumps:** each jump rises about 2 m (was 1.2 m); the double jump adds a second one of the same height.
- **Head / weak point bonus per weapon** (owner, 2026-11-12): pistol x2; shotgun, rifle, staffs and sword x1.5. **Perks can raise it**: the weapon tree node "Marksman" adds +0.25 per rank (3 ranks) to every weapon, staff and sword included (provisional numbers). Spell projectiles get no head bonus unless a spell defines one.
- **Fireball shockwave:** pushes enemies away from the blast (strength scaled by QTE power).
- **Player:** 100 health (regenerates 2/s after 5 s without damage), 100 mana (6/s after 1.5 s), speed 750, dash 7 m in 0.18 s every 1.2 s.
- **QTE:** 4 keys, 1 gesture, 4 s in real time (raised from 3 s by the owner), world at 10% speed.
- **Staff:** Apprentice staff 12 damage every 0.35 s, no mana cost. Ember staff 22 fire damage every 0.6 s and burns.
- **Guns:** pistol 18 damage, 12 rounds, 4 spare magazines; shotgun 8 pellets of 10, 6 rounds, strong up close; rifle automatic, 14 damage, 30 rounds, stronger far away. Headshots: pistol x2, shotgun and rifle x1.5.
- **Enemies:** past orc 60 health, melee 12; future orc 70 health, ranged 9; brute (sub-boss placeholder) 320 health, melee 28.
- **Status effects:** burn 32 damage over 4 s; slow 50% for 4 s; chill 30% for 3 s; shock 40% for 1.5 s; health potion 60 over 10 s; injection 35 at once; enchant +25% gun damage for 20 s.
- **Skill trees:** 6 nodes each, 1-2 points per rank, up to 3 ranks.
- Every spell number in `Spells.json`.

### Elemental build-up (owner's spec, 2026-11-12)
Every enemy has three independent bars: **fire, lightning, ice**. A valid hit of an element fills its bar; a full bar starts that element's status effect.
- **Rules for each bar:** its own threshold, duration, immunity time and decay. After a while without new build-up the bar drains little by little. When the status starts the bar goes back to zero; while the status runs that element does not build up again; after it ends there can be an immunity time before it builds up again. The three bars never affect each other. No reactions between elements yet.
- **Ignite (fire, sustained damage):** fire damage at fixed time steps for the status duration. Sources: fireball, fire wall, flamethrower (on its 0.3 s damage ticks), the ember staff, the elemental sword and a fire-enchanted gun.
- **Shock (lightning, interruption):** an electric discharge (a small hit of lightning damage) and the enemy's reaction: **stun** (stops moving and attacking for the duration, its attack is cancelled), **interrupt** (only cancels the attack it was winding up) or **none**. Sources: lightning bolt (every enemy it passes through, once each), lightning rune (enemies in its blast radius, so Expanded Sigil applies), static orb, the elemental sword and a lightning-enchanted gun.
- **Frost (ice, slow and control):** the enemy's reaction: **freeze** (cannot move or attack for the duration), **slow** (a strong slow) or **none**. Sources: the **ice floor only** among spells (low build-up on each of its ticks, so standing on it fills the bar slowly and an ice-enchanted gun finishes it faster), the elemental sword and an ice-enchanted gun. The ice wall and the ice shield build up nothing. The ice floor's own slow (50%, Deep Freeze 55/60/65%, cap 80%, QTE) is unchanged. **Slows never stack:** when the ice floor and Frost both slow an enemy, only the strongest counts.
- **Per enemy (no global multipliers by enemy type):** each enemy can set, per element, its damage taken, its build-up taken (separately, so they balance apart), its threshold, the status duration, the immunity time, the decay, and its reaction (or immunity to the status: an enemy can be immune to Shock and still take lightning damage). Values not set by an enemy fall back to defaults in `Game.json`.
- **Per source:** each spell has its own build-up per hit or per tick (`BuildUp` in `Spells.json`); each weapon has its own build-up per element (`FireBuildUp`, `LightningBuildUp`, `IceBuildUp` in `Weapons.json`). An unenchanted gun builds up nothing; the apprentice staff (arcane) builds up nothing. One shot counts once per enemy: the eight pellets of a shotgun shot give one build-up to each enemy they hit.
- **Weak point bonus:** a weapon hit on the head or on a weak point multiplies its build-up (`WeakPointBuildUpMult`), only once even if the head is also a weak point. It does not change the head damage bonus.
- **Visuals:** not decided yet (Niagara, shaders or something per enemy). The code only sends events (build-up changed, status started, status ended) that each enemy's look can use later. A debug view (`gb.ShowElemental 1` in the console) prints the bars over enemies for testing; it is not the game's indicator.
- **Removed by the owner (2026-11-12):** the small effects every elemental hit used to apply (burn on fire hits, the 40% slow on lightning hits, the enchant's chill). The bar's status effect is now the only elemental effect. The electric grenade builds up lightning instead of applying the old shock (architect).

- Spells cost **mana**.

toolUseResult.newString:
### Elemental build-up (owner's spec, 2026-11-12)
Every enemy has three independent bars: **fire, lightning, ice**. A valid hit of an element fills its bar; a full bar starts that element's status effect.
- **Rules for each bar:** its own threshold, duration, immunity time and decay. After a while without new build-up the bar drains little by little. When the status starts the bar goes back to zero; while the status runs that element does not build up again; after it ends there can be an immunity time before it builds up again. The three bars never affect each other. No reactions between elements yet.
- **Ignite (fire, sustained damage):** fire damage at fixed time steps for the status duration. Sources: fireball, fire wall, flamethrower (on its 0.3 s damage ticks), the ember staff, the elemental sword and a fire-enchanted gun.
- **Shock (lightning, interruption):** an electric discharge (a small hit of lightning damage) and the enemy's reaction: **stun** (stops moving and attacking for the duration, its attack is cancelled), **interrupt** (only cancels the attack it was winding up) or **none**. Sources: lightning bolt (every enemy it passes through, once each), lightning rune (enemies in its blast radius, so Expanded Sigil applies), static orb, the elemental sword and a lightning-enchanted gun.
- **Frost (ice, slow and control):** the enemy's reaction: **freeze** (cannot move or attack for the duration), **slow** (a strong slow) or **none**. Sources: the **ice floor only** among spells (low build-up on each of its ticks, so standing on it fills the bar slowly and an ice-enchanted gun finishes it faster), the elemental sword and an ice-enchanted gun. The ice wall and the ice shield build up nothing. The ice floor's own slow (50%, Deep Freeze 55/60/65%, cap 80%, QTE) is unchanged. **Slows never stack:** when the ice floor and Frost both slow an enemy, only the strongest counts.
- **Per enemy (no global multipliers by enemy type):** each enemy can set, per element, its damage taken, its build-up taken (separately, so they balance apart), its threshold, the status duration, the immunity time, the decay, and its reaction (or immunity to the status: an enemy can be immune to Shock and still take lightning damage). Values not set by an enemy fall back to defaults in `Game.json`.
- **Per source:** each spell has its own build-up per hit or per tick (`BuildUp` in `Spells.json`); each weapon has its own build-up per element (`FireBuildUp`, `LightningBuildUp`, `IceBuildUp` in `Weapons.json`). An unenchanted gun builds up nothing; the apprentice staff (arcane) builds up nothing. One shot counts once per enemy: the eight pellets of a shotgun shot give one build-up to each enemy they hit.
- **Weak point bonus:** a weapon hit on the head or on a weak point multiplies its build-up (`WeakPointBuildUpMult`), only once even if the head is also a weak point. It does not change the head damage bonus.
- **Visuals:** not decided yet (Niagara, shaders or something per enemy). The code only sends events (build-up changed, status started, status ended) that each enemy's look can use later. A debug view (`gb.ShowElemental 1` in the console) prints the bars over enemies for testing; it is not the game's indicator.
- **Removed by the owner (2026-11-12):** the small effects every elemental hit used to apply (burn on fire hits, the 40% slow on lightning hits, the enchant's chill). The bar's status effect is now the only elemental effect. The electric grenade builds up lightning instead of applying the old shock (architect).

### General
- Spells cost **mana**.

# Owner's spec: elemental build-up and status effects (2026-11-12)

> Verbatim from the owner (Spanish), pasted into the architect chat. English summary: GDD v0.22, section 6 "Elemental build-up".
> The architect read the code first, listed the conflicts with the existing systems, and asked two questions; the owner's answers:
> 1. The existing small effects on every elemental hit (fire burn, the lightning 40% slow already named "Shock", the ice enchant's chill): **remove them all**. The bar's status effect is the only elemental effect; the ice floor keeps its zone slow.
> 2. The elemental sword and the ember staff: **both build up** their element.

---

Implementación del sistema de efectos de estado elementales

Necesitamos incorporar un sistema de acumulación elemental (Elemental Build-Up) y efectos de estado para Fuego, Rayo y Hielo al juego existente.

IMPORTANTE: El proyecto ya cuenta con hechizos, armas, encantamientos elementales, enemigos, daño, cooldowns, maná, QTE y perks funcionando. Antes de implementar, revisar la arquitectura actual y reutilizar los sistemas existentes. No reconstruir ni reemplazar mecánicas que ya funcionan correctamente.

El objetivo es implementar primero el funcionamiento de los efectos de estado y dejar los valores numéricos configurables para balancearlos posteriormente.

## 1. Sistema general de acumulación elemental
Cada enemigo debe gestionar independientemente tres acumuladores: `FireBuildUp`, `LightningBuildUp`, `IceBuildUp`.
Cada acumulador aumenta cuando el enemigo recibe un impacto válido de su elemento correspondiente. Cuando una acumulación alcanza el umbral configurado, se activa su efecto de estado.
Reglas generales:
- Cada elemento posee su propia acumulación, umbral, duración, inmunidad temporal y velocidad de decaimiento.
- Si transcurre un período configurable sin recibir acumulación de un elemento, su barra comienza a disminuir progresivamente.
- Al activarse un efecto, la acumulación correspondiente vuelve a cero.
- Mientras el efecto esté activo, no se acumula nuevamente ese mismo elemento.
- Después de finalizar, puede existir un período configurable de inmunidad temporal antes de permitir una nueva acumulación.
- Los tres elementos deben funcionar independientemente.
- Los efectos de daño y control deben ser independientes de la velocidad de fotogramas.
- Evitar aplicaciones duplicadas de acumulación por un único impacto o evento de daño.

No es necesario implementar todavía reacciones especiales entre diferentes elementos.

## 2. Configuración individual por enemigo
No utilizar multiplicadores globales de resistencia por categoría de enemigo, como un multiplicador universal para élites o bosses.
Cada enemigo debe poder definir individualmente:
- Resistencia o vulnerabilidad al daño de Fuego, Rayo y Hielo.
- Resistencia o vulnerabilidad a la acumulación de cada elemento.
- Umbral de acumulación elemental.
- Duración efectiva de cada estado.
- Inmunidad temporal después de un estado.
- Si es inmune a un estado específico.
- Qué reacción realiza cuando se activa cada efecto.

Por ejemplo, una valquiria podría resistir mucho el fuego y ser vulnerable al rayo, mientras que otro boss podría presentar exactamente lo contrario.
Igualmente, un enemigo puede recibir daño eléctrico sin ser susceptible a una interrupción completa.
Mantener independientes las resistencias al daño y las resistencias a la acumulación, para poder balancearlas por separado.
Utilizar valores por defecto únicamente como respaldo para enemigos sin configuración específica, no como sustituto de sus características individuales.

## 3. Estado de Fuego — Ignite
Identidad: daño sostenido.
Al alcanzar el umbral de acumulación de fuego, el enemigo entra en estado `Ignite`.
Comportamiento:
- Aplica daño periódico durante una duración configurable.
- El daño se calcula mediante intervalos de tiempo definidos, no por frame.
- No debe activar nuevos estados Ignite mientras el actual siga activo.
- Al finalizar, se aplica la inmunidad temporal configurada para ese enemigo.
- Cada enemigo puede tener diferentes resistencias, duración y daño de quemadura.

Fuentes de acumulación: Fireball, Fire Wall, Flamethrower, armas encantadas con Fuego.
Cada fuente debe tener su propio valor de acumulación.
Por ejemplo, Flamethrower debería poder acumular más fuego mediante exposición continua que un único impacto de Fireball, pero los valores exactos se determinarán posteriormente.
Compatibilidad: revisar el efecto de quemadura que ya posee Fireball y reutilizarlo o integrarlo con Ignite para evitar dos sistemas de DOT que se dupliquen accidentalmente. No cambiar silenciosamente su comportamiento actual; documentar cualquier ajuste necesario.

## 4. Estado de Rayo — Shock
Identidad: interrupción y control inmediato.
Al alcanzar el umbral de acumulación eléctrica, el enemigo entra en estado `Shock`.
Comportamiento:
- Produce una descarga eléctrica.
- Puede interrumpir el ataque o habilidad que el enemigo esté ejecutando.
- Puede provocar una breve reacción de aturdimiento o desestabilización.
- La reacción debe ser configurable individualmente por enemigo.
- Determinados enemigos pueden resistir el aturdimiento, pero recibir una interrupción menor.
- Otros pueden ser completamente inmunes al efecto de control.
- Al finalizar, debe respetarse la inmunidad temporal configurada para evitar interrupciones continuas.

No establecer reglas universales que obliguen a todos los bosses a reaccionar de la misma manera.
Fuentes de acumulación: Lightning Bolt, Lightning Rune, Static Orb, armas encantadas con Rayo.
Cada fuente posee su propia acumulación configurable.
En Lightning Rune, el radio de detección que activa la trampa y el radio de su explosión son diferentes. La acumulación se aplica a los enemigos alcanzados por la explosión, respetando el comportamiento actual de `Expanded Sigil`.

## 5. Estado de Hielo — Frost
Identidad: ralentización y control prolongado.
Al alcanzar el umbral de acumulación de hielo, el enemigo entra en estado `Frost`.
Comportamiento:
- Puede congelar temporalmente al enemigo o reducir considerablemente su velocidad.
- La reacción se configura individualmente por enemigo.
- Algunos enemigos podrán quedar inmovilizados.
- Otros sufrirán una ralentización fuerte.
- Determinados enemigos podrán resistir el congelamiento o ser inmunes.
- Al finalizar, se respeta la inmunidad temporal correspondiente.

Fuentes de acumulación: Ice Floor, armas encantadas con Hielo.
Por ahora, Ice Floor será el único hechizo que aplique acumulación de hielo.
Ice Wall e Ice Shield no deben aplicar acumulación elemental.
La acumulación generada por Ice Floor debe ser relativamente baja y configurable.
La intención es que Ice Floor pueda acumular hielo gradualmente mientras los enemigos permanecen dentro de su zona, pero que el jugador pueda completar esa acumulación más rápidamente utilizando un arma encantada con Hielo.
Compatibilidad con Ice Floor:
- La ralentización base actual es del 50%.
- `Deep Freeze` la aumenta a 55%, 60% y 65% según su nivel.
- El límite máximo configurado es del 80%.
- Ya existe interacción con el QTE.

No reemplazar ni modificar esos comportamientos.
La ralentización adicional de Frost no debe sumarse de manera descontrolada a la ralentización de Ice Floor. Utilizar una regla consistente, como aplicar el efecto de ralentización más fuerte, respetando los límites correspondientes.

## 6. Acumulación específica de cada hechizo
No establecer un valor fijo de acumulación para todos los hechizos de un mismo elemento.
Cada hechizo debe poder configurar individualmente:
- Elemento aplicado.
- Acumulación por impacto o tick válido.
- Intervalo entre aplicaciones de acumulación, cuando corresponda.
- Si puede aplicar acumulación o no.

Los hechizos continuos deben utilizar intervalos controlados para impedir que la acumulación dependa de los FPS.
En particular, Flamethrower ya utiliza intervalos de daño de 0,3 segundos. Procurar reutilizar esos eventos para aplicar acumulación, evitando introducir procesos de daño adicionales innecesarios.
Mantener intactas sus demás mecánicas existentes, incluidos el consumo inicial de maná, el consumo por segundo, el QTE, la canalización mientras se mantiene la tecla y la interrupción por daño fuerte.

## 7. Acumulación mediante Weapon Enchant
Las armas encantadas deben aplicar acumulación del elemento seleccionado.
Elementos disponibles: Fire, Lightning, Ice.
Reglas:
- Las armas sin encantamiento no aplican acumulación elemental, salvo que alguna tenga esa propiedad explícitamente configurada.
- Cada impacto válido de un arma encantada puede contribuir a la acumulación.
- El valor de acumulación debe poder configurarse por arma y elemento.
- La acumulación debe respetar las resistencias del enemigo.
- Los distintos tipos de armas pueden tener valores diferentes.
- Evitar acumulación excesiva causada por múltiples impactos, especialmente en armas como la escopeta.

No modificar el daño o funcionamiento de las armas si no es necesario para integrar este sistema.

## 8. Bonificación por Headshots y puntos débiles
Los impactos realizados con armas encantadas sobre la cabeza o sobre un punto débil del enemigo deben conceder una bonificación configurable de acumulación elemental.
Reglas:
- Un headshot válido obtiene la bonificación.
- Un impacto sobre un punto débil definido por el enemigo obtiene la misma bonificación.
- Los puntos débiles no tienen que ser necesariamente la cabeza.
- Si la cabeza también está marcada como punto débil, la bonificación no debe aplicarse dos veces.
- El modificador debe poder configurarse y balancearse posteriormente.
- La bonificación afecta a la acumulación elemental; no modificar automáticamente el multiplicador de daño crítico o de headshot existente.

Utilizar el sistema actual de hitboxes o detección de puntos débiles si ya existe. No crear uno paralelo innecesariamente.

## 9. Configuración mediante datos
Mantener la implementación compatible con la arquitectura actual del proyecto.
Aprovechar `Spells.json`, `Game.json` y las configuraciones existentes de enemigos y armas, cuando corresponda.
Los parámetros deberían ser editables sin modificar la lógica del sistema.
Incluir, según corresponda: `BuildUpAmount`, `BuildUpThreshold`, `BuildUpDecayRate`, `DecayDelay`, `StatusDuration`, `StatusImmunityDuration`, `StatusEffectType`, `StatusDamage`, `StatusTickInterval`, `StatusSlowAmount`, `StatusControlReaction`, `ElementalResistance`, `HeadshotBuildUpBonus`, `WeakPointBuildUpBonus`.
Los nombres son orientativos. Adaptarlos a las convenciones existentes del proyecto.
Si un parámetro ya existe con otro nombre, reutilizarlo.
Los valores iniciales pueden ser provisionales para comprobar que los tres estados funcionan, pero deben quedar claramente identificados como pendientes de balanceo.

## 10. Efectos visuales
Por ahora, implementar únicamente los eventos y estados necesarios para que el sistema pueda comunicarse con los efectos visuales posteriores.
La representación visual se decidirá más adelante y podrá utilizar Niagara, shaders o efectos particulares por enemigo.
No crear todavía un indicador visual universal obligatorio.
Cada enemigo deberá poder responder visualmente a: acumulación elemental, activación del estado, estado activo, finalización del estado.
La ausencia de efectos visuales definitivos no debe impedir que funcione el sistema.

## 11. Compatibilidad y rendimiento
Este sistema debe funcionar correctamente con múltiples enemigos simultáneamente, considerando que el juego tendrá hordas.
Priorizar:
- Reutilización de los eventos de daño existentes.
- Ausencia de comprobaciones costosas por frame cuando puedan utilizarse eventos o intervalos.
- Gestión independiente de los estados de cada enemigo.
- Evitar aplicaciones duplicadas durante explosiones, proyectiles penetrantes y ataques continuos.
- Limpieza de estados y procesos temporales cuando un enemigo muere o es destruido.
- Respeto de las mecánicas actuales de daño, resistencias, cooldowns, QTE y perks.
- Separación entre lógica de combate y representación visual.

No implementar todavía nuevas sinergias elementales, perks adicionales ni mecánicas fuera de este alcance.

## 12. Pruebas de funcionamiento
Antes de considerar terminada la implementación, comprobar:
1. Un hechizo de fuego acumula Ignite y activa el DOT al alcanzar su umbral.
2. Lightning Bolt puede acumular Shock sobre varios enemigos atravesados sin duplicar impactos.
3. Ice Floor acumula Frost gradualmente mientras el enemigo permanece en el área.
4. Un arma encantada puede completar una acumulación iniciada por un hechizo.
5. Un headshot o impacto sobre un punto débil aplica la bonificación correspondiente una sola vez.
6. Dos enemigos diferentes pueden tener resistencias y umbrales distintos para el mismo elemento.
7. Un enemigo puede ser inmune a Shock sin volverse inmune al daño eléctrico.
8. Las inmunidades temporales evitan la aplicación continua del mismo estado.
9. La acumulación disminuye correctamente cuando deja de aplicarse el elemento.
10. Los efectos funcionan con varios enemigos simultáneamente sin errores ni degradaciones evidentes.
11. Ice Floor conserva sus valores de ralentización, perk Deep Freeze y QTE.
12. Flamethrower conserva sus intervalos, consumo de maná y condiciones de interrupción.
13. El nuevo Ignite no duplica accidentalmente la quemadura existente de Fireball.

## 13. Resultado esperado
Implementar un sistema elemental modular, reutilizable y configurable que permita:
- Acumular efectos elementales mediante hechizos y armas encantadas.
- Aplicar Ignite, Shock y Frost.
- Configurar resistencias y respuestas individualmente por enemigo.
- Recompensar headshots y ataques a puntos débiles.
- Ajustar posteriormente todos los valores durante el balanceo.
- Añadir sinergias y nuevos perks en una etapa posterior sin reconstruir el sistema.

Prioridad principal: conservar la estabilidad del juego existente, implementar correctamente las tres mecánicas y evitar complejidad innecesaria durante el Game Jam.
Antes de realizar cambios, revisar las clases, archivos y sistemas actuales. Si alguna mecánica existente entra en conflicto con esta especificación, identificarla y explicar la solución propuesta. Al finalizar, resumir qué archivos se modificaron, qué quedó configurable y qué pruebas se realizaron.

# Owner's spec: elemental build-up and status effects (2026-11-12)

> Verbatim from the owner (Spanish), pasted into the architect chat. English summary: GDD v0.22, section 6 "Elemental build-up".
> The architect read the code first, listed the conflicts with the existing systems, and asked two questions; the owner's answers:
> 1. The existing small effects on every elemental hit (fire burn, the lightning 40% slow already named "Shock", the ice enchant's chill): **remove them all**. The bar's status effect is the only elemental effect; the ice floor keeps its zone slow.
> 2. The elemental sword and the ember staff: **both build up** their element.

---

Implementación del sistema de efectos de estado elementales

Necesitamos incorporar un sistema de acumulación elemental (Elemental Build-Up) y efectos de estado para Fuego, Rayo y Hielo al juego existente.

IMPORTANTE: El proyecto ya cuenta con hechizos, armas, encantamientos elementales, enemigos, daño, cooldowns, maná, QTE y perks funcionando. Antes de implementar, revisar la arquitectura actual y reutilizar los sistemas existentes. No reconstruir ni reemplazar mecánicas que ya funcionan correctamente.

El objetivo es implementar primero el funcionamiento de los efectos de estado y dejar los valores numéricos configurables para balancearlos posteriormente.

## 1. Sistema general de acumulación elemental
Cada enemigo debe gestionar independientemente tres acumuladores: `FireBuildUp`, `LightningBuildUp`, `IceBuildUp`.
Cada acumulador aumenta cuando el enemigo recibe un impacto válido de su elemento correspondiente. Cuando una acumulación alcanza el umbral configurado, se activa su efecto de estado.
Reglas generales:
- Cada elemento posee su propia acumulación, umbral, duración, inmunidad temporal y velocidad de decaimiento.
- Si transcurre un período configurable sin recibir acumulación de un elemento, su barra comienza a disminuir progresivamente.
- Al activarse un efecto, la acumulación correspondiente vuelve a cero.
- Mientras el efecto esté activo, no se acumula nuevamente ese mismo elemento.
- Después de finalizar, puede existir un período configurable de inmunidad temporal antes de permitir una nueva acumulación.
- Los tres elementos deben funcionar independientemente.
- Los efectos de daño y control deben ser independientes de la velocidad de fotogramas.
- Evitar aplicaciones duplicadas de acumulación por un único impacto o evento de daño.

No es necesario implementar todavía reacciones especiales entre diferentes elementos.

## 2. Configuración individual por enemigo
No utilizar multiplicadores globales de resistencia por categoría de enemigo, como un multiplicador universal para élites o bosses.
Cada enemigo debe poder definir individualmente:
- Resistencia o vulnerabilidad al daño de Fuego, Rayo y Hielo.
- Resistencia o vulnerabilidad a la acumulación de cada elemento.
- Umbral de acumulación elemental.
- Duración efectiva de cada estado.
- Inmunidad temporal después de un estado.
- Si es inmune a un estado específico.
- Qué reacción realiza cuando se activa cada efecto.

Por ejemplo, una valquiria podría resistir mucho el fuego y ser vulnerable al rayo, mientras que otro boss podría presentar exactamente lo contrario.
Igualmente, un enemigo puede recibir daño eléctrico sin ser susceptible a una interrupción completa.
Mantener independientes las resistencias al daño y las resistencias a la acumulación, para poder balancearlas por separado.
Utilizar valores por defecto únicamente como respaldo para enemigos sin configuración específica, no como sustituto de sus características individuales.

## 3. Estado de Fuego — Ignite
Identidad: daño sostenido.
Al alcanzar el umbral de acumulación de fuego, el enemigo entra en estado `Ignite`.
Comportamiento:
- Aplica daño periódico durante una duración configurable.
- El daño se calcula mediante intervalos de tiempo definidos, no por frame.
- No debe activar nuevos estados Ignite mientras el actual siga activo.
- Al finalizar, se aplica la inmunidad temporal configurada para ese enemigo.
- Cada enemigo puede tener diferentes resistencias, duración y daño de quemadura.

Fuentes de acumulación: Fireball, Fire Wall, Flamethrower, armas encantadas con Fuego.
Cada fuente debe tener su propio valor de acumulación.
Por ejemplo, Flamethrower debería poder acumular más fuego mediante exposición continua que un único impacto de Fireball, pero los valores exactos se determinarán posteriormente.

## 4. Estado de Rayo — Shock
Identidad: interrupción y control inmediato.
Al alcanzar el umbral de acumulación eléctrica, el enemigo entra en estado `Shock`.
Comportamiento:
- Produce una descarga eléctrica.
- Puede interrumpir el ataque o habilidad que el enemigo esté ejecutando.
- Puede provocar una breve reacción de aturdimiento o desestabilización.
- La reacción debe ser configurable individualmente por enemigo.
- Determinados enemigos pueden resistir el aturdimiento, pero recibir una interrupción menor.
- Otros pueden ser completamente inmunes al efecto de control.
- Al finalizar, debe respetarse la inmunidad temporal configurada para evitar interrupciones continuas.

## 5. Estado de Hielo — Frost
Identidad: ralentización y control prolongado.

Comportamiento:
- Puede congelar temporalmente al enemigo o reducir considerablemente su velocidad.
- La reacción se configura individualmente por enemigo.
- Algunos enemigos podrán quedar inmovilizados.
- Otros sufrirán una ralentización fuerte.
- Determinados enemigos podrán resistir el congelamiento o ser inmunes.
- Al finalizar, se respeta la inmunidad temporal correspondiente.
