+La intención es que Ice Floor pueda acumular hielo gradualmente mientras los enemigos permanecen dentro de su zona, pero que el jugador pueda completar esa acumulación más rápidamente utilizando un arma encantada con Hielo.
+Compatibilidad con Ice Floor:
+- La ralentización base actual es del 50%.
+- `Deep Freeze` la aumenta a 55%, 60% y 65% según su nivel.
+- El límite máximo configurado es del 80%.
+- Ya existe interacción con el QTE.
+No reemplazar ni modificar esos comportamientos.

+La ralentización adicional de Frost no debe sumarse de manera descontrolada a la ralentización de Ice Floor. Utilizar una regla consistente, como aplicar el efecto de ralentización más fuerte, respetando los límites correspondientes.
+## 6. Acumulación específica de cada hechizo
+No establecer un valor fijo de acumulación para todos los hechizos de un mismo elemento.
+Cada hechizo debe poder configurar individualmente:
+- Elemento aplicado.
+- Acumulación por impacto o tick válido.
+- Intervalo entre aplicaciones de acumulación, cuando corresponda.
+- Si puede aplicar acumulación o no.
+Los hechizos continuos deben utilizar intervalos controlados para impedir que la acumulación dependa de los FPS.
+En particular, Flamethrower ya utiliza intervalos de daño de 0,3 segundos. Procurar reutilizar esos eventos para aplicar acumulación, evitando introducir procesos de daño adicionales innecesarios.

+Mantener intactas sus demás mecánicas existentes, incluidos el consumo inicial de maná, el consumo por segundo, el QTE, la canalización mientras se mantiene la tecla y la interrupción por daño fuerte.
+## 7. Acumulación mediante Weapon Enchant
+Las armas encantadas deben aplicar acumulación del elemento seleccionado.
+Elementos disponibles: Fire, Lightning, Ice.
+Reglas:
+- Las armas sin encantamiento no aplican acumulación elemental, salvo que alguna tenga esa propiedad explícitamente configurada.
+- Cada impacto válido de un arma encantada puede contribuir a la acumulación.
+- El valor de acumulación debe poder configurarse por arma y elemento.
+- La acumulación debe respetar las resistencias del enemigo.
+- Los distintos tipos de armas pueden tener valores diferentes.
+- Evitar acumulación excesiva causada por múltiples impactos, especialmente en armas como la escopeta.
+No modificar el daño o funcionamiento de las armas si no es necesario para integrar este sistema.
+## 8. Bonificación por Headshots y puntos débiles
+Los impactos realizados con armas encantadas sobre la cabeza o sobre un punto débil del enemigo deben conceder una bonificación configurable de acumulación elemental.
+Reglas:
+- Un headshot válido obtiene la bonificación.
+- Un impacto sobre un punto débil definido por el enemigo obtiene la misma bonificación.
+- Los puntos débiles no tienen que ser necesariamente la cabeza.
+- Si la cabeza también está marcada como punto débil, la bonificación no debe aplicarse dos veces.
+- El modificador debe poder configurarse y balancearse posteriormente.
+- La bonificación afecta a la acumulación elemental; no modificar automáticamente el multiplicador de daño crítico o de headshot existente.
+Utilizar el sistema actual de hitboxes o detección de puntos débiles si ya existe. No crear uno paralelo innecesariamente.
+## 9. Configuración mediante datos
+Mantener la implementación compatible con la arquitectura actual del proyecto.
+Aprovechar `Spells.json`, `Game.json` y las configuraciones existentes de enemigos y armas, cuando corresponda.
+Los parámetros deberían ser editables sin modificar la lógica del sistema.

+Incluir, según corresponda: `BuildUpAmount`, `BuildUpThreshold`, `BuildUpDecayRate`, `DecayDelay`, `StatusDuration`, `StatusImmunityDuration`, `StatusEffectType`, `StatusDamage`, `StatusTickInterval`, `StatusSlowAmount`, `StatusControlReaction`, `ElementalResistance`, `HeadshotBuildUpBonus`, `WeakPointBuildUpBonus`.
+Los nombres son orientativos. Adaptarlos a las convenciones existentes del proyecto.
+Si un parámetro ya existe con otro nombre, reutilizarlo.
+Los valores iniciales pueden ser provisionales para comprobar que los tres estados funcionan, pero deben quedar claramente identificados como pendientes de balanceo.
+## 10. Efectos visuales
+Por ahora, implementar únicamente los eventos y estados necesarios para que el sistema pueda comunicarse con los efectos visuales posteriores.
+La representación visual se decidirá más adelante y podrá utilizar Niagara, shaders o efectos particulares por enemigo.
+No crear todavía un indicador visual universal obligatorio.
+Cada enemigo deberá poder responder visualmente a: acumulación elemental, activación del estado, estado activo, finalización del estado.
+La ausencia de efectos visuales definitivos no debe impedir que funcione el sistema.
+## 11. Compatibilidad y rendimiento
+Este sistema debe funcionar correctamente con múltiples enemigos simultáneamente, considerando que el juego tendrá hordas.
+Priorizar:
+- Reutilización de los eventos de daño existentes.
+- Ausencia de comprobaciones costosas por frame cuando puedan utilizarse eventos o intervalos.
+- Gestión independiente de los estados de cada enemigo.
+- Evitar aplicaciones duplicadas durante explosiones, proyectiles penetrantes y ataques continuos.
+- Limpieza de estados y procesos temporales cuando un enemigo muere o es destruido.
+- Respeto de las mecánicas actuales de daño, resistencias, cooldowns, QTE y perks.
+- Separación entre lógica de combate y representación visual.
+No implementar todavía nuevas sinergias elementales, perks adicionales ni mecánicas fuera de este alcance.
+## 12. Pruebas de funcionamiento
+Antes de considerar terminada la implementación, comprobar:
+1. Un hechizo de fuego acumula Ignite y activa el DOT al alcanzar su umbral.
+2. Lightning Bolt puede acumular Shock sobre varios enemigos atravesados sin duplicar impactos.
+3. Ice Floor acumula Frost gradualmente mientras el enemigo permanece en el área.
+4. Un arma encantada puede completar una acumulación iniciada por un hechizo.
+5. Un headshot o impacto sobre un punto débil aplica la bonificación correspondiente una sola vez.
+6. Dos enemigos diferentes pueden tener resistencias y umbrales distintos para el mismo elemento.
+7. Un enemigo puede ser inmune a Shock sin volverse inmune al daño eléctrico.
+8. Las inmunidades temporales evitan la aplicación continua del mismo estado.
+9. La acumulación disminuye correctamente cuando deja de aplicarse el elemento.
+10. Los efectos funcionan con varios enemigos simultáneamente sin errores ni degradaciones evidentes.
+11. Ice Floor conserva sus valores de ralentización, perk Deep Freeze y QTE.
+12. Flamethrower conserva sus intervalos, consumo de maná y condiciones de interrupción.
+13. El nuevo Ignite no duplica accidentalmente la quemadura existente de Fireball.
+## 13. Resultado esperado
+Implementar un sistema elemental modular, reutilizable y configurable que permita:
+- Acumular efectos elementales mediante hechizos y armas encantadas.
+- Aplicar Ignite, Shock y Frost.
+- Configurar resistencias y respuestas individualmente por enemigo.
+- Recompensar headshots y ataques a puntos débiles.
+- Ajustar posteriormente todos los valores durante el balanceo.
+- Añadir sinergias y nuevos perks en una etapa posterior sin reconstruir el sistema.
+Prioridad principal: conservar la estabilidad del juego existente, implementar correctamente las tres mecánicas y evitar complejidad innecesaria durante el Game Jam.

+Antes de realizar cambios, revisar las clases, archivos y sistemas actuales. Si alguna mecánica existente entra en conflicto con esta especificación, identificarla y explicar la solución propuesta. Al finalizar, resumir qué archivos se modificaron, qué quedó configurable y qué pruebas se realizaron.

# Rules for every implementer on Glyphbound (read first)

You implement one part of **Glyphbound**, a first-person RPG shooter for the Epic AI MegaJam 2026, in **Unreal Engine 5.9.0**, C++. The architect (another agent) wrote the public headers; you write the implementation. Several implementers work **at the same time** on different folders, so the rules about file ownership matter.

## Read before writing
1. `C:\GameJam\Design\ARCHITECTURE.md` (the whole file, it is short).
2. `C:\GameJam\Design\GDD.md`: the sections named in your task.
3. In `C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\Source\Glyphbound\`: `Core/GBTypes.h`, `Core/GBStatNames.h`, `Core/GBPlaceholder.h`, `Data/GBDataTypes.h`, `Data/GBDataSubsystem.h`, `Stats/GBStatsComponent.h`, `Stats/GBAttributeComponent.h`, `Combat/GBCombatLibrary.h`, plus every header your task names. The header comments are the specification: implement what they say.

## File ownership
- You own ONLY the files listed in your task. Create the `.cpp` for each header you own, and new files inside your folders if you need them.
- **Never edit a file you do not own.** If you need something from another module that its header does not offer, code against what exists, and write the request in your final report.
- In headers you own you MAY add includes, private/protected members, helper methods and extra public methods. You MUST NOT remove, rename or change the signature of anything already public there: other implementers are calling it right now.
- Do not edit `Glyphbound.Build.cs`, `.uproject`, or `Config/`. Module dependencies available: Core, CoreUObject, Engine, InputCore, EnhancedInput, Json, JsonUtilities, AIModule, NavigationSystem, Slate, SlateCore, UMG. If you need another one, say so in your report.

## Hard rules
- **Do not build, do not run the Editor, do not run tests, do not commit, do not launch other agents.** The architect integrates and builds after everyone finishes. Write code that compiles: check every engine API you are not sure about in the engine source at `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9\Engine\Source` (grep the header). UE 5.9 is newer than your training data; when in doubt, look.
- **No gameplay numbers in code.** Damage, costs, cooldowns, speeds, sizes, durations, timings and counts come from the JSON data through `UGBDataSubsystem` and `UGBStatsComponent` (stat names in `Core/GBStatNames.h`). If you need a number that has no stat yet, add a named constant `inline const FName` in a header YOU own (same style as `GBStatNames.h`), read it from the data with a sensible default, put its value in your JSON file, and list it in your report. Layout pixels and pure visual offsets may be code constants.
- Everything must work when a JSON entry is missing: use the default argument, log a warning with `UE_LOG(LogGB, Warning, ...)`, never crash, never divide by zero.
- No binary assets. 3D placeholders: `GBPlaceholder::SetupShape` (engine basic shapes). Pixel-art placeholders: `UGBPixelSpriteLibrary` (sprites described as text in `Sprites.json`). Art rule (GDD 3): medieval and magic things are pixel-art sprites; cyberpunk things are 3D.
- No custom collision channels or profiles that need config: use the engine's default channels and filter by team in code (`UGBCombatLibrary::AreHostile`).
- Do not keep pointers to definitions (`FGBSpellDefinition*`...) across frames; keep the id.
- A class member must never be named `Cast` (it hides the engine's `Cast<T>()`).
- All on-screen text in English. Comments in English, and only where they explain a decision or a non-obvious rule. ASCII only.
- Includes are relative to the module root: `#include "Stats/GBStatsComponent.h"`. Every `.cpp` includes its own header first. Every header with reflected types includes its `.generated.h` last.
- Keep it simple. This is a 4-day jam: clear, short code that works beats clever code. No speculative abstractions beyond what the headers define.

## Tests (only if your task asks for them)
- Pure logic only, no world, no assets: `IMPLEMENT_SIMPLE_AUTOMATION_TEST(FName, "Glyphbound.<Area>.<Name>", EAutomationTestFlags::EditorContext | EAutomationTestFlags::EngineFilter)` inside `#if WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS`, in `Tests/GB<Area>Tests.cpp`.
- Each test must be able to fail: before writing it, ask which wrong implementation would still pass it. No tests that copy a constant, check that a field exists, or read source text.
- A test name must never be a prefix of another test name (`A.B` next to `A.B.C` silently stops `A.B`).
- Keep them few and fast (the whole suite must stay well under 30 s).

## Final report (your last message, plain text, short)
1. Files you wrote or changed.
2. Anything in your headers that you added to the public API.
3. Requests for other modules (what you needed and did not find).
4. Design values you had to invent (they will be marked provisional in the GDD).
5. Risks: API calls you could not verify, things you expect may not compile, behavior you are unsure about.
# Task: six new spell perks, a param cap, and a hold-to-sustain flamethrower

Project: **Glyphbound** (Unreal Engine 5.9.0, C++), in `Glyphbound/`. Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `Prompts/implementer_rules.md` first (you DO build and run things in this task; the rest of "Hard rules" applies). One build or run at a time. Do not open the Unreal Editor. Do not commit.

Owner's requests, GDD v0.20 (changelog; section 5 "New perks"; section 6 fire row; section 18 "Sustained spells" and "New spell perks"). The architect decided the design below; implement exactly this.

## 1. Six new nodes in `Glyphbound/Content/Data/Skills.json` (data only)
All `"Tree": "Spell"`, `"Cost": 1`, `"MaxRank": 3`, no `Requires`. Columns follow the existing spell tree (column 0 fire, 1 lightning, 2 ice). Modifier ops behave like the existing nodes (`Multiply` stacks linearly per rank: 1.15 at rank 1, 1.30 at rank 2, 1.45 at rank 3).

| Id | DisplayName | Description | Modifier per rank | Column | Row |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Spell_FireWallDuration` | Lingering Flames | +15% fire wall duration per rank. | `Spell.FireWall.Duration` Multiply 1.15 | 0 | 2 |
| `Spell_FlamethrowerDamage` | Intense Heat | +12% flamethrower damage per rank. | `Spell.Flamethrower.DamagePerSecond` Multiply 1.12 | 0 | 3 |
| `Spell_RuneRadius` | Expanded Sigil | +10% lightning rune blast radius per rank. | `Spell.LightningRune.Radius` Multiply 1.10 | 1 | 3 |
| `Spell_OrbDuration` | Persistent Charge | +15% static orb duration per rank. | `Spell.StaticOrb.Duration` Multiply 1.15 | 1 | 4 |
| `Spell_ShieldDuration` | Enduring Guard | +15% ice shield duration per rank. | `Spell.IceShield.Duration` Multiply 1.15 | 2 | 1 |
| `Spell_IceFloorSlow` | Deep Freeze | Ice floor slows 5 points more per rank (up to 80%). | `Spell.IceFloor.EffectStrength` Add 0.1 | 2 | 2 |

Before writing them, check in the code that: the rune's blast radius is the `Radius` param (not `TriggerRadius`), the orb and shield read `Duration` through the resolved cast (so `Spell.<Id>.Duration` modifiers reach them), and the ice floor's slow is `Slow` (`MoveSpeed` Multiply 0.5) scaled by `EffectStrength` so that strength +0.1 = +5 points of slow (read how `UGBStatusEffectComponent` applies a strength scale to a Multiply modifier). If any of these is not true, tell me in the report and pick the param that matches the description; do not change gameplay code to make the table fit.
Check that the spell tree screen still fits (`AGBHUD::DrawSkillTrees`, now 5 rows in the spell tree) at 1280x720: boxes must stay readable (names abbreviated is fine); if a row would overflow the panel, fix the layout math, not the data.

## 2. Validation of modifier keys (so a typo can never silently do nothing)
In `UGBDataSubsystem`, after loading (and after `gb.ReloadData`), check every skill node modifier (and armor / status effect modifiers if they share the struct and it is cheap): a key `Spell.<Id>.<Param>` must name an existing spell id (or `All`) and a param that exists in that spell's `Params` (for `All`: in at least one spell). Otherwise `UE_LOG(LogGB, Warning, ...)` naming the node and the key. Do the same for `Weapon.<Id>.<Stat>` only if the weapon stat names are easy to enumerate; otherwise skip weapons and say so. The smoke run fails on LogGB warnings, so a wrong key in item 1 will show up.

## 3. Optional `Cap` per spell parameter
- `Data/GBDataTypes.h`: the scaled param struct gets `float Cap = 0.f;` (0 = no cap; comment: upper limit applied after QTE scaling AND modifiers).
- `Spells/GBSpellTypes.cpp`, `GBSpell::ResolveCast` and the single-param resolve below it: after `ApplySpellModifiers`, if `Cap > 0`, `Value = FMath::Min(Value, Cap)`. Put the clamp in one small pure function and use it in both places.
- `Spells.json`, `IceFloor.Params.EffectStrength`: add `"Cap": 1.6` (= 80% slow).
- Test `Glyphbound.Spells.ParamCap` (pure): a value above the cap is clamped, below is unchanged, cap 0 means no cap. Check the name rule.

## 4. Flamethrower: runs while its key is held
Today `AGBSpell_Beam` runs for `Duration` or until the slot key is pressed again (`UGBSpellbookComponent::TryCastSlot` -> `OnCastReleased`), and only `ETriggerEvent::Started` is bound for spell slots (`AGBPlayerCharacter`, around `BindAction(S->SpellSlot1 ...)`).
New behavior, as data-driven beam params (document them in the header's param list):
- `HoldToSustain` (1 = the beam runs only while the cast key is held; 0 = old behavior). Flamethrower: 1.
- `MinDuration` seconds: the beam always runs at least this long (so a cast whose key was released during the QTE is not wasted). Flamethrower: 0.75.
- `Duration` <= 0 means no time limit. Flamethrower: remove `Duration` from its params, or set Base/Min/Max 0 (no limit). Its QTE power still scales `DamagePerSecond` as today.
- `ManaPerSecond`: flamethrower 15 (Base/Min/Max 15, ScaledBy None). The beam already stops when mana runs out; keep that. `ManaCost` (paid at the cast): flamethrower 10.
- Description in `Spells.json`: "A stream of fire from your hand. Hold the spell key to keep it going; it drains mana."
- Pure function (testable), static on `AGBSpell_Beam`: `static bool ShouldBeamContinue(bool bHoldToSustain, bool bKeyHeld, float Elapsed, float MinDuration, float MaxDuration);` -> false when `MaxDuration > 0 && Elapsed >= MaxDuration`; true while `Elapsed < MinDuration`; otherwise `!bHoldToSustain || bKeyHeld`. Use it each damage tick (or each frame) to decide whether to `EndSpell()`. Test `Glyphbound.Spells.BeamHold` covering: held keeps going, released after the minimum stops, released before the minimum keeps going, max duration stops even if held, hold mode off ignores the key. Mana running out is handled where it is today.
- Is the key held? Add `bool AGBPlayerCharacter::IsSpellInputHeld(FName SpellId) const`: finds the loadout slot of that spell (`UGBSpellbookComponent`) and reads the current value of that slot's input action from Enhanced Input (keyboard / mouse: slot 1 = right click, slots 2-5 = keys 1-4; gamepad: L1 for slot 1, L2 + face button for slots 2-5: read the action value, which already includes those mappings and chords). If the caster is not the player, or the spell is not in the loadout, treat it as held (the beam then ends by mana, death, switch or MinDuration rules). The beam asks its caster through this function.
- `TryCastSlot`'s "press again to stop" stays (harmless: with hold mode the key is held while it runs).
- Weapon switch, death and the QTE rules are unchanged; the cooldown still starts at the cast.

## 5. Smoke script (`Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`)
- Where it unlocks a node: also log the number of skill nodes loaded (`SMOKE skills loaded=%d`), expect 18.
- Add a short step that casts the flamethrower with the QTE off while the smoke script cannot hold a key (the player's key is not held in an automated run): log `SMOKE flamethrower started=%d` right after the cast and `SMOKE flamethrower after=%.2fs alive=%d` about 1.5 s later; with the key not held it must have stopped after `MinDuration` (alive=0), else `UE_LOG(LogGB, Error, ...)`. Put it where it does not disturb later steps (the end is fine).

## Verification (all must be true when you finish)
1. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
2. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1 -Target Glyphbound` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
3. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -MinTests 29` passes.
4. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1` ends with `Smoke: done=True crashed=False LogGB errors=0 timedOut=False`, with `SMOKE path check passed`, the new SMOKE lines, and no `LogGB` warning. Open `5_skills.png` and say whether the spell tree fits and is readable.
Never make an error disappear by deleting behavior. All JSON files stay valid. No gameplay numbers in code.

## Final report (plain text)
1. The four result lines verbatim, plus the new SMOKE lines.
2. What you changed, with file names; the result of the checks asked in item 1.
3. Your description of `5_skills.png`.
4. Anything you could not do as described, and why.
5. What a person should check by playing.

# Task: elemental build-up (Ignite, Shock, Frost) on enemies

Project: **Glyphbound** (Unreal Engine 5.9.0, C++), in `Glyphbound/`. Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `Prompts/implementer_rules.md` first (you DO build and run things in this task; the rest of "Hard rules" applies). One build or run at a time. Do not open the Unreal Editor. Do not commit.

Owner's spec, GDD v0.22: read `Design/GDD.md` section 6 "Elemental build-up" and the v0.22 lines of section 18 "Numbers". The owner's original text (Spanish) is `Prompts/feedback8_elemental_spec_owner.md`; this brief is the architect's design for it. **Implement exactly this.** If something here contradicts the code you find, say so in the report and pick the option that keeps existing behavior.

Summary: every enemy gets three independent bars (fire, lightning, ice). Hits with a build-up value fill the bar of their element; a full bar starts a status (Ignite = damage over time, Shock = discharge + stun or interrupt, Frost = freeze or strong slow), then an immunity time. Everything is data. The old small per-hit effects (Burn, the old Shock slow, Chill) are removed.

---

## 1. Shared types and names

### `Core/GBTypes.h`
- `FGBDamageInfo`: add three fields (UPROPERTY like the others, with a one-line comment each):
  - `float BuildUp = 0.f;` raw elemental build-up this hit adds to the target's bar of `Element` (before the target's resistance and the weak point bonus).
  - `float WeakPointBuildUpMult = 1.f;` multiplies `BuildUp` once when `bHeadshot` is true (weapon hits only).
  - `int32 BuildUpEventId = 0;` hits that share an id add build-up to one target only once (shotgun pellets of one shot); 0 = no dedupe.
- `EGBModOp`: add `MultiplyMin` at the end. Meaning: like `Multiply`, but among all `MultiplyMin` modifiers on one stat **only the lowest counts** (the strongest slow wins); that one multiplies with the plain `Multiply` ones. Update the comment at the top of `Stats/GBStatsComponent.h`.

### `Stats/GBStatsComponent.cpp`
- `AddModifiers`: `MultiplyMin` is scaled around 1 exactly like `Multiply`.
- `ApplyModifiers`: keep the lowest `MultiplyMin` value (none if there is no such modifier) and multiply it into the product. Order and Override behavior unchanged.

### `Core/GBStatNames.h`
- `GBStat::BuildUp` ("BuildUp"): spell param and item stat, raw build-up per hit or per tick.
- `GBStat::WeakPointBuildUpMult` ("WeakPointBuildUpMult"): weapon stat; when a weapon does not have it, `Game.json` `WeakPointBuildUpMult` is the default.
- A small namespace `GBElemental` with:
  - `int32 ElementIndex(EGBElement Element)`: Fire 0, Lightning 1, Ice 2, anything else -1. `constexpr int32 NumElements = 3;`.
  - `EGBElement IndexToElement(int32 Index)`.
  - Per-element key tables (built once, `static const FName[3]` or a function returning a const FName from a static array; never `FName(*FString::Printf(...))` per call):
    `DamageTaken(i)` -> `FireDamageTaken`, `LightningDamageTaken`, `IceDamageTaken`;
    `BuildUpTaken(i)` -> `FireBuildUpTaken`...; `Threshold(i)` -> `FireBuildUpThreshold`...; `DecayDelay(i)` -> `FireBuildUpDecayDelay`...; `DecayRate(i)` -> `FireBuildUpDecayRate`...; `StatusDuration(i)` -> `FireStatusDuration`...; `StatusImmunity(i)` -> `FireStatusImmunity`...; `Reaction(i)` -> `FireStatusReaction`, `LightningStatusReaction`, `IceStatusReaction` (enemy `Strings`); `WeaponBuildUp(i)` -> `FireBuildUp`, `LightningBuildUp`, `IceBuildUp` (weapon stats).
  - Single keys: `IgniteDamageMult`, `ShockDischargeDamage`, `FrostSlow`.
  - Default prefix: the default of enemy key `K` is `Game.json` `"ElementalDefault.K"` (Values for numbers, Strings for reactions). Provide `FName DefaultKey(FName Key)` built once per key (cache in a small static TMap or per-table static arrays).
  - Reaction names: `Ignite`, `Stun`, `Interrupt`, `Freeze`, `Slow`, `None`; status effect id `Ignite`.

---

## 2. Pure logic: `Combat/GBBuildUpMeter.h` / `.cpp` (new files, no UObjects)

```cpp
enum class EGBBuildUpPhase : uint8 { Building, Active, Immune };

struct FGBBuildUpConfig
{
	float Threshold = 0.f;        // <= 0: this bar never fills (element disabled for this enemy)
	float BuildUpTaken = 1.f;     // multiplier on incoming build-up (resistance < 1, vulnerability > 1, 0 = immune)
	float DecayDelay = 0.f;       // seconds without build-up before the bar drains
	float DecayRate = 0.f;        // points per second
	float StatusDuration = 0.f;
	float ImmunityDuration = 0.f;
};

struct FGBBuildUpMeter
{
	float Value = 0.f;
	EGBBuildUpPhase Phase = EGBBuildUpPhase::Building;
	float PhaseTimeRemaining = 0.f;
	float TimeSinceBuildUp = 0.f;

	/** Adds Amount * BuildUpTaken while Building. Returns true when this add filled the bar: Value goes to 0 and the phase to Active for StatusDuration. Ignored (false) when not Building, Amount <= 0, BuildUpTaken <= 0 or Threshold <= 0. Resets the decay delay. Full means Value >= Threshold - 1e-4 (float tolerance, so exactly the threshold counts). */
	bool Add(float Amount, const FGBBuildUpConfig& Config);

	/** Advances time; returns a bit mask of EGBBuildUpEvent (ValueChanged, StatusEnded, ImmunityEnded). */
	uint8 Advance(float DeltaTime, const FGBBuildUpConfig& Config);

	/** Building with an empty bar: nothing to tick. */
	bool IsIdle() const;
};
```
`Advance` rules (frame-rate independent: one step of 1.0 s must give the same result as ten steps of 0.1 s):
- **Building:** `Before = TimeSinceBuildUp; TimeSinceBuildUp += Dt;` if `Value > 0`: decay time this step = `max(0, TimeSinceBuildUp - max(Before, DecayDelay))`; `Value = max(0, Value - DecayRate * DecayTime)`; ValueChanged if it changed.
- **Active:** `PhaseTimeRemaining -= Dt`; when `<= 1e-4`: StatusEnded; if `ImmunityDuration > 0` -> Immune with `PhaseTimeRemaining = ImmunityDuration + PhaseTimeRemaining` (carry the overshoot) else Building. A status with `StatusDuration <= 0` ends on the next Advance.
- **Immune:** `PhaseTimeRemaining -= Dt`; when `<= 1e-4` -> Building, ImmunityEnded.

```cpp
/** Remembers the last 8 build-up events of one target, so one event (a shotgun shot) counts once: the biggest amount of that event wins. */
struct FGBBuildUpEventLog
{
	/** Returns how much of Amount to really add: all of it for a new id (or id 0); for a known id only the part above what that id already added (0 if smaller). */
	float Accept(int32 EventId, float Amount);
	// ring of 8 {Id, Amount}; a new id overwrites the oldest entry
};
```

## 3. Component: `Combat/GBElementalStatusComponent.h` / `.cpp` (new)

`UGBElementalStatusComponent : UActorComponent` (ClassGroup Glyphbound, BlueprintSpawnableComponent). Combat logic only, no visuals. Public API:
```cpp
static UGBElementalStatusComponent* Find(const AActor* Actor);
/** Raw build-up of Element (Fire / Lightning / Ice; others ignored), before the owner's BuildUpTaken. EventId != 0 is deduped through FGBBuildUpEventLog. Returns true if it started the status. */
bool AddBuildUp(EGBElement Element, float Amount, int32 EventId, AActor* Instigator);
float GetBuildUp(EGBElement Element) const;
float GetThreshold(EGBElement Element) const;
EGBBuildUpPhase GetPhase(EGBElement Element) const;
float GetPhaseTimeRemaining(EGBElement Element) const;
bool IsStatusActive(EGBElement Element) const;
FName GetReaction(EGBElement Element) const;   // see below
void ClearAll();

// Events for the look of each enemy (Niagara, shaders... later). No visuals here.
FGBOnBuildUpChanged OnBuildUpChanged;          // (EGBElement, float Value, float Threshold)
FGBOnElementalStatusStarted OnStatusStarted;   // (EGBElement, FName Reaction, float Duration)
FGBOnElementalStatusEnded OnStatusEnded;       // (EGBElement)
FGBOnElementalStatusEnded OnImmunityEnded;     // (EGBElement)
```
Declare the delegates (native multicast) in the header.

**Config per element** (read when needed, never cached across a data reload): numbers from the owner's `UGBStatsComponent::GetStat(Key, Default)` where `Default = Data->GetGameValue(GBElemental::DefaultKey(Key), 0)` (so an enemy's `Stats` value wins, and modifiers can change it later); the reaction from the owner's enemy definition `Strings` (`AGBEnemyCharacter::GetDefinition()`), else `Data->GetGameString(DefaultKey, "None")`. Valid reactions: Fire `Ignite` / `None`; Lightning `Stun` / `Interrupt` / `None`; Ice `Freeze` / `Slow` / `None`. An unknown text logs one warning (once per enemy id and element) and counts as `None`. Reaction `None` = immune to that status: no build-up is added (the damage itself is untouched). A missing default (threshold 0) disables that bar; log one warning per key, once.

**Tick:** `PrimaryComponentTick.TickInterval = Game.json ElementalTickInterval` (set in BeginPlay; default 0.1). Tick is enabled only while some meter is not idle (enable in AddBuildUp / StartStatus, disable when all three are idle). Each tick: `Advance` each meter with DeltaTime (the engine passes the real elapsed time), broadcast `OnBuildUpChanged` on ValueChanged, and on StatusEnded / ImmunityEnded run the end logic and broadcast.

**Status start** (when `Add` returns true), with `Duration = <E>StatusDuration`, `Instigator` = the one whose hit filled the bar:
- **Fire, `Ignite`:** `UGBStatusEffectComponent::ApplyEffect("Ignite", Instigator, DurationScale = Duration / IgniteDefinition.Duration (guard against 0), StrengthScale = IgniteDamageMult)`. The Ignite effect is data in `StatusEffects.json` (ticks of fire damage through `DealDamage`, so FireDamageTaken applies and it never adds build-up).
- **Lightning:** first the discharge: if `ShockDischargeDamage > 0`, `UGBCombatLibrary::DealDamage(Owner, Info)` with that amount, Element Lightning, the instigator, `SourceId "Shock"`, `BuildUp 0`. # Task: elemental build-up (Ignite, Shock, Frost) on enemies

Project: **Glyphbound** (Unreal Engine 5.9.0, C++), in `Glyphbound/`. Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `Prompts/implementer_rules.md` first (you DO build and run things in this task; the rest of "Hard rules" applies). One build or run at a time. Do not open the Unreal Editor. Do not commit.

Owner's spec, GDD v0.22: read `Design/GDD.md` section 6 "Elemental build-up" and the v0.22 lines of section 18 "Numbers". The owner's original text (Spanish) is `Prompts/feedback8_elemental_spec_owner.md`; this brief is the architect's design for it. **Implement exactly this.** If something here contradicts the code you find, say so in the report and pick the option that keeps existing behavior.

Summary: every enemy gets three independent bars (fire, lightning, ice). Hits with a build-up value fill the bar of their element; a full bar starts a status (Ignite = damage over time, Shock = discharge + stun or interrupt, Frost = freeze or strong slow), then an immunity time. Everything is data. The old small per-hit effects (Burn, the old Shock slow, Chill) are removed.

---

## 1. Shared types and names

### `Core/GBTypes.h`
- `FGBDamageInfo`: add three fields (UPROPERTY like the others, with a one-line comment each):
  - `float BuildUp = 0.f;` raw elemental build-up this hit adds to the target's bar of `Element` (before the target's resistance and the weak point bonus).
  - `float WeakPointBuildUpMult = 1.f;` multiplies `BuildUp` once when `bHeadshot` is true (weapon hits only).
  - `int32 BuildUpEventId = 0;` hits that share an id add build-up to one target only once (shotgun pellets of one shot); 0 = no dedupe.
- `EGBModOp`: add `MultiplyMin` at the end. Meaning: like `Multiply`, but among all `MultiplyMin` modifiers on one stat **only the lowest counts** (the strongest slow wins); that one multiplies with the plain `Multiply` ones. Update the comment at the top of `Stats/GBStatsComponent.h`.

### `Stats/GBStatsComponent.cpp`
- `AddModifiers`: `MultiplyMin` is scaled around 1 exactly like `Multiply`.
- `ApplyModifiers`: keep the lowest `MultiplyMin` value (none if there is no such modifier) and multiply it into the product. Order and Override behavior unchanged.

### `Core/GBStatNames.h`
- `GBStat::BuildUp` ("BuildUp"): spell param and item stat, raw build-up per hit or per tick.
- `GBStat::WeakPointBuildUpMult` ("WeakPointBuildUpMult"): weapon stat; when a weapon does not have it, `Game.json` `WeakPointBuildUpMult` is the default.
- A small namespace `GBElemental` with:
  - `int32 ElementIndex(EGBElement Element)`: Fire 0, Lightning 1, Ice 2, anything else -1. `constexpr int32 NumElements = 3;`.
  - `EGBElement IndexToElement(int32 Index)`.
  - Per-element key tables (built once, `static const FName[3]` or a function returning a const FName from a static array; never `FName(*FString::Printf(...))` per call):
    `DamageTaken(i)` -> `FireDamageTaken`, `LightningDamageTaken`, `IceDamageTaken`;
    `BuildUpTaken(i)` -> `FireBuildUpTaken`...; `Threshold(i)` -> `FireBuildUpThreshold`...; `DecayDelay(i)` -> `FireBuildUpDecayDelay`...; `DecayRate(i)` -> `FireBuildUpDecayRate`...; `StatusDuration(i)` -> `FireStatusDuration`...; `StatusImmunity(i)` -> `FireStatusImmunity`...; `Reaction(i)` -> `FireStatusReaction`, `LightningStatusReaction`, `IceStatusReaction` (enemy `Strings`); `WeaponBuildUp(i)` -> `FireBuildUp`, `LightningBuildUp`, `IceBuildUp` (weapon stats).
  - Single keys: `IgniteDamageMult`, `ShockDischargeDamage`, `FrostSlow`.
  - Default prefix: the default of enemy key `K` is `Game.json` `"ElementalDefault.K"` (Values for numbers, Strings for reactions). Provide `FName DefaultKey(FName Key)` built once per key (cache in a small static TMap or per-table static arrays).
  - Reaction names: `Ignite`, `Stun`, `Interrupt`, `Freeze`, `Slow`, `None`; status effect id `Ignite`.

---

## 2. Pure logic: `Combat/GBBuildUpMeter.h` / `.cpp` (new files, no UObjects)

```cpp
enum class EGBBuildUpPhase : uint8 { Building, Active, Immune };

struct FGBBuildUpConfig
{
	float Threshold = 0.f;        // <= 0: this bar never fills (element disabled for this enemy)
	float BuildUpTaken = 1.f;     // multiplier on incoming build-up (resistance < 1, vulnerability > 1, 0 = immune)
	float DecayDelay = 0.f;       // seconds without build-up before the bar drains
	float DecayRate = 0.f;        // points per second
	float StatusDuration = 0.f;
	float ImmunityDuration = 0.f;
};

struct FGBBuildUpMeter
{
	float Value = 0.f;
	EGBBuildUpPhase Phase = EGBBuildUpPhase::Building;
	float PhaseTimeRemaining = 0.f;
	float TimeSinceBuildUp = 0.f;

	/** Adds Amount * BuildUpTaken while Building. Returns true when this add filled the bar: Value goes to 0 and the phase to Active for StatusDuration. Ignored (false) when not Building, Amount <= 0, BuildUpTaken <= 0 or Threshold <= 0. Resets the decay delay. Full means Value >= Threshold - 1e-4 (float tolerance, so exactly the threshold counts). */
	bool Add(float Amount, const FGBBuildUpConfig& Config);

	/** Advances time; returns a bit mask of EGBBuildUpEvent (ValueChanged, StatusEnded, ImmunityEnded). */
	uint8 Advance(float DeltaTime, const FGBBuildUpConfig& Config);

	/** Building with an empty bar: nothing to tick. */
	bool IsIdle() const;
};
```
`Advance` rules (frame-rate independent: one step of 1.0 s must give the same result as ten steps of 0.1 s):
- **Building:** `Before = TimeSinceBuildUp; TimeSinceBuildUp += Dt;` if `Value > 0`: decay time this step = `max(0, TimeSinceBuildUp - max(Before, DecayDelay))`; `Value = max(0, Value - DecayRate * DecayTime)`; ValueChanged if it changed.
- **Active:** `PhaseTimeRemaining -= Dt`; when `<= 1e-4`: StatusEnded; if `ImmunityDuration > 0` -> Immune with `PhaseTimeRemaining = ImmunityDuration + PhaseTimeRemaining` (carry the overshoot) else Building. A status with `StatusDuration <= 0` ends on the next Advance.
- **Immune:** `PhaseTimeRemaining -= Dt`; when `<= 1e-4` -> Building, ImmunityEnded.

```cpp
/** Remembers the last 8 build-up events of one target, so one event (a shotgun shot) counts once: the biggest amount of that event wins. */
struct FGBBuildUpEventLog
{
	/** Returns how much of Amount to really add: all of it for a new id (or id 0); for a known id only the part above what that id already added (0 if smaller). */
	float Accept(int32 EventId, float Amount);
	// ring of 8 {Id, Amount}; a new id overwrites the oldest entry
};
```

## 3. Component: `Combat/GBElementalStatusComponent.h` / `.cpp` (new)

`UGBElementalStatusComponent : UActorComponent` (ClassGroup Glyphbound, BlueprintSpawnableComponent). Combat logic only, no visuals. Public API:
```cpp
static UGBElementalStatusComponent* Find(const AActor* Actor);
/** Raw build-up of Element (Fire / Lightning / Ice; others ignored), before the owner's BuildUpTaken. EventId != 0 is deduped through FGBBuildUpEventLog. Returns true if it started the status. */
bool AddBuildUp(EGBElement Element, float Amount, int32 EventId, AActor* Instigator);
float GetBuildUp(EGBElement Element) const;
float GetThreshold(EGBElement Element) const;
EGBBuildUpPhase GetPhase(EGBElement Element) const;
float GetPhaseTimeRemaining(EGBElement Element) const;
bool IsStatusActive(EGBElement Element) const;
FName GetReaction(EGBElement Element) const;   // see below
void ClearAll();

// Events for the look of each enemy (Niagara, shaders... later). No visuals here.
FGBOnBuildUpChanged OnBuildUpChanged;          // (EGBElement, float Value, float Threshold)
FGBOnElementalStatusStarted OnStatusStarted;   // (EGBElement, FName Reaction, float Duration)
FGBOnElementalStatusEnded OnStatusEnded;       // (EGBElement)
FGBOnElementalStatusEnded OnImmunityEnded;     // (EGBElement)
```
Declare the delegates (native multicast) in the header.

**Config per element** (read when needed, never cached across a data reload): numbers from the owner's `UGBStatsComponent::GetStat(Key, Default)` where `Default = Data->GetGameValue(GBElemental::DefaultKey(Key), 0)` (so an enemy's `Stats` value wins, and modifiers can change it later); the reaction from the owner's enemy definition `Strings` (`AGBEnemyCharacter::GetDefinition()`), else `Data->GetGameString(DefaultKey, "None")`. Valid reactions: Fire `Ignite` / `None`; Lightning `Stun` / `Interrupt` / `None`; Ice `Freeze` / `Slow` / `None`. An unknown text logs one warning (once per enemy id and element) and counts as `None`. Reaction `None` = immune to that status: no build-up is added (the damage itself is untouched). A missing default (threshold 0) disables that bar; log one warning per key, once.

**Tick:** `PrimaryComponentTick.TickInterval = Game.json ElementalTickInterval` (set in BeginPlay; default 0.1). Tick is enabled only while some meter is not idle (enable in AddBuildUp / StartStatus, disable when all three are idle). Each tick: `Advance` each meter with DeltaTime (the engine passes the real elapsed time), broadcast `OnBuildUpChanged` on ValueChanged, and on StatusEnded / ImmunityEnded run the end logic and broadcast.

**Status start** (when `Add` returns true), with `Duration = <E>StatusDuration`, `Instigator` = the one whose hit filled the bar:
- **Fire, `Ignite`:** `UGBStatusEffectComponent::ApplyEffect("Ignite", Instigator, DurationScale = Duration / IgniteDefinition.Duration (guard against 0), StrengthScale = IgniteDamageMult)`. The Ignite effect is data in `StatusEffects.json` (ticks of fire damage through `DealDamage`, so FireDamageTaken applies and it never adds build-up).
- **Lightning:** first the discharge: if `ShockDischargeDamage > 0`, `UGBCombatLibrary::DealDamage(Owner, Info)` with that amount, Element Lightning, the instigator, `SourceId "Shock"`, `BuildUp 0`. If that killed the owner, stop here. The reaction (`Stun` / `Interrupt`) is done by the enemy through `OnStatusStarted` (below).
- **Ice, `Slow`:** `Stats->AddModifiers("Elemental.Frost", { MoveSpeed, MultiplyMin, 1 - clamp(FrostSlow, 0, 0.95) })`. `Freeze` is done by the enemy through `OnStatusStarted`.
- Then broadcast `OnStatusStarted(Element, Reaction, Duration)` (also for Ignite and Slow) and `OnBuildUpChanged` (value 0).

**Status end:** Fire: `RemoveEffect("Ignite")` (in case a data reload changed durations); Ice: `RemoveModifiers("Elemental.Frost")`; broadcast `OnStatusEnded`.

**Death and cleanup:** bind the owner's attribute `OnDeath` in BeginPlay -> `ClearAll()` (meters reset, Frost modifier removed, tick off). EndPlay: unbind and remove the Frost modifier. No timers survive the owner.

## 4. Damage path: `Combat/GBCombatLibrary.h/.cpp`
- `static int32 NewBuildUpEventId();` global counter, never returns 0.
- `static bool IsWeakPointHit(const AActor* Target, const FVector& HitLocation);` today: `AGBEnemyCharacter::IsHeadshotLocation`. The one place to add other weak points later; a head that is also a weak point is still one hit, so the bonus can never apply twice. Update the header comment.
- `ApplyWeakPointBonus`: `Info.bHeadshot = IsWeakPointHit(...)`; only if `bHeadshot && WeakPointMult > 1` multiply `Amount`. Returns `bHeadshot`. (Today all weapons have mult >= 1.5, so nothing visible changes; it decouples the build-up bonus from the damage bonus.)
- `static float ApplyBuildUp(AActor* Target, const FGBDamageInfo& Info);` returns the raw amount sent. Does nothing unless `Info.BuildUp > 0`, the element is Fire / Lightning / Ice, `CanDamage(Info.Instigator, Target)`, and the target has a `UGBElementalStatusComponent`. Amount = `BuildUp * (bHeadshot ? max(1, WeakPointBuildUpMult) : 1)`; calls `AddBuildUp(Element, Amount, BuildUpEventId, Instigator)`.
- `DealDamage`: right after a hit that dealt damage (`Dealt > 0`, where `OnDamageDealt` is broadcast), call `ApplyBuildUp(Target, FinalInfo)`. Leave the generic `OnHitEffect` code as it is (the ice floor's slow still uses on-hit effects).
- `Stats/GBAttributeComponent.cpp` `ApplyDamage`: multiply by the element's `<E>DamageTaken` stat (default 1) next to `DamageTaken`.

# Task: elemental build-up (Ignite, Shock, Frost) on enemies

Project: **Glyphbound** (Unreal Engine 5.9.0, C++), in `Glyphbound/`. Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `Prompts/implementer_rules.md` first (you DO build and run things in this task; the rest of "Hard rules" applies). One build or run at a time. Do not open the Unreal Editor. Do not commit.

Owner's spec, GDD v0.22: read `Design/GDD.md` section 6 "Elemental build-up" and the v0.22 lines of section 18 "Numbers". The owner's original text (Spanish) is `Prompts/feedback8_elemental_spec_owner.md`; this brief is the architect's design for it. **Implement exactly this.** If something here contradicts the code you find, say so in the report and pick the option that keeps existing behavior.

Summary: every enemy gets three independent bars (fire, lightning, ice). Hits with a build-up value fill the bar of their element; a full bar starts a status (Ignite = damage over time, Shock = discharge + stun or interrupt, Frost = freeze or strong slow), then an immunity time. Everything is data. The old small per-hit effects (Burn, the old Shock slow, Chill) are removed.

---

## 1. Shared types and names

### `Core/GBTypes.h`
- `FGBDamageInfo`: add three fields (UPROPERTY like the others, with a one-line comment each):
  - `float BuildUp = 0.f;` raw elemental build-up this hit adds to the target's bar of `Element` (before the target's resistance and the weak point bonus).
  - `float WeakPointBuildUpMult = 1.f;` multiplies `BuildUp` once when `bHeadshot` is true (weapon hits only).
  - `int32 BuildUpEventId = 0;` hits that share an id add build-up to one target only once (shotgun pellets of one shot); 0 = no dedupe.
- `EGBModOp`: add `MultiplyMin` at the end. Meaning: like `Multiply`, but among all `MultiplyMin` modifiers on one stat **only the lowest counts** (the strongest slow wins); that one multiplies with the plain `Multiply` ones. Update the comment at the top of `Stats/GBStatsComponent.h`.

### `Stats/GBStatsComponent.cpp`
- `AddModifiers`: `MultiplyMin` is scaled around 1 exactly like `Multiply`.
- `ApplyModifiers`: keep the lowest `MultiplyMin` value (none if there is no such modifier) and multiply it into the product. Order and Override behavior unchanged.

### `Core/GBStatNames.h`
- `GBStat::BuildUp` ("BuildUp"): spell param and item stat, raw build-up per hit or per tick.
- `GBStat::WeakPointBuildUpMult` ("WeakPointBuildUpMult"): weapon stat; when a weapon does not have it, `Game.json` `WeakPointBuildUpMult` is the default.
- A small namespace `GBElemental` with:
  - `int32 ElementIndex(EGBElement Element)`: Fire 0, Lightning 1, Ice 2, anything else -1. `constexpr int32 NumElements = 3;`.
  - `EGBElement IndexToElement(int32 Index)`.
  - Per-element key tables (built once, `static const FName[3]` or a function returning a const FName from a static array; never `FName(*FString::Printf(...))` per call):
    `DamageTaken(i)` -> `FireDamageTaken`, `LightningDamageTaken`, `IceDamageTaken`;
    `BuildUpTaken(i)` -> `FireBuildUpTaken`...; `Threshold(i)` -> `FireBuildUpThreshold`...; `DecayDelay(i)` -> `FireBuildUpDecayDelay`...; `DecayRate(i)` -> `FireBuildUpDecayRate`...; `StatusDuration(i)` -> `FireStatusDuration`...; `StatusImmunity(i)` -> `FireStatusImmunity`...; `Reaction(i)` -> `FireStatusReaction`, `LightningStatusReaction`, `IceStatusReaction` (enemy `Strings`); `WeaponBuildUp(i)` -> `FireBuildUp`, `LightningBuildUp`, `IceBuildUp` (weapon stats).
  - Single keys: `IgniteDamageMult`, `ShockDischargeDamage`, `FrostSlow`.
  - Default prefix: the default of enemy key `K` is `Game.json` `"ElementalDefault.K"` (Values for numbers, Strings for reactions). Provide `FName DefaultKey(FName Key)` built once per key (cache in a small static TMap or per-table static arrays).
  - Reaction names: `Ignite`, `Stun`, `Interrupt`, `Freeze`, `Slow`, `None`; status effect id `Ignite`.

---

## 2. Pure logic: `Combat/GBBuildUpMeter.h` / `.cpp` (new files, no UObjects)

```cpp
enum class EGBBuildUpPhase : uint8 { Building, Active, Immune };

struct FGBBuildUpConfig
{
	float Threshold = 0.f;        // <= 0: this bar never fills (element disabled for this enemy)
	float BuildUpTaken = 1.f;     // multiplier on incoming build-up (resistance < 1, vulnerability > 1, 0 = immune)
	float DecayDelay = 0.f;       // seconds without build-up before the bar drains
	float DecayRate = 0.f;        // points per second
	float StatusDuration = 0.f;
	float ImmunityDuration = 0.f;
};

struct FGBBuildUpMeter
{
	float Value = 0.f;
	EGBBuildUpPhase Phase = EGBBuildUpPhase::Building;
	float PhaseTimeRemaining = 0.f;
	float TimeSinceBuildUp = 0.f;

	/** Adds Amount * BuildUpTaken while Building. Returns true when this add filled the bar: Value goes to 0 and the phase to Active for StatusDuration. Ignored (false) when not Building, Amount <= 0, BuildUpTaken <= 0 or Threshold <= 0. Resets the decay delay. Full means Value >= Threshold - 1e-4 (float tolerance, so exactly the threshold counts). */
	bool Add(float Amount, const FGBBuildUpConfig& Config);

	/** Advances time; returns a bit mask of EGBBuildUpEvent (ValueChanged, StatusEnded, ImmunityEnded). */
	uint8 Advance(float DeltaTime, const FGBBuildUpConfig& Config);

	/** Building with an empty bar: nothing to tick. */
	bool IsIdle() const;
};
```
`Advance` rules (frame-rate independent: one step of 1.0 s must give the same result as ten steps of 0.1 s):
- **Building:** `Before = TimeSinceBuildUp; TimeSinceBuildUp += Dt;` if `Value > 0`: decay time this step = `max(0, TimeSinceBuildUp - max(Before, DecayDelay))`; `Value = max(0, Value - DecayRate * DecayTime)`; ValueChanged if it changed.
- **Active:** `PhaseTimeRemaining -= Dt`; when `<= 1e-4`: StatusEnded; if `ImmunityDuration > 0` -> Immune with `PhaseTimeRemaining = ImmunityDuration + PhaseTimeRemaining` (carry the overshoot) else Building. A status with `StatusDuration <= 0` ends on the next Advance.
- **Immune:** `PhaseTimeRemaining -= Dt`; when `<= 1e-4` -> Building, ImmunityEnded.

```cpp
/** Remembers the last 8 build-up events of one target, so one event (a shotgun shot) counts once: the biggest amount of that event wins. */
struct FGBBuildUpEventLog
{
	/** Returns how much of Amount to really add: all of it for a new id (or id 0); for a known id only the part above what that id already added (0 if smaller). */
	float Accept(int32 EventId, float Amount);
	// ring of 8 {Id, Amount}; a new id overwrites the oldest entry
};
```

## 3. Component: `Combat/GBElementalStatusComponent.h` / `.cpp` (new)

`UGBElementalStatusComponent : UActorComponent` (ClassGroup Glyphbound, BlueprintSpawnableComponent). Combat logic only, no visuals. Public API:
```cpp
static UGBElementalStatusComponent* Find(const AActor* Actor);
/** Raw build-up of Element (Fire / Lightning / Ice; others ignored), before the owner's BuildUpTaken. EventId != 0 is deduped through FGBBuildUpEventLog. Returns true if it started the status. */
bool AddBuildUp(EGBElement Element, float Amount, int32 EventId, AActor* Instigator);
float GetBuildUp(EGBElement Element) const;
float GetThreshold(EGBElement Element) const;
EGBBuildUpPhase GetPhase(EGBElement Element) const;
float GetPhaseTimeRemaining(EGBElement Element) const;
bool IsStatusActive(EGBElement Element) const;
FName GetReaction(EGBElement Element) const;   // see below
void ClearAll();

// Events for the look of each enemy (Niagara, shaders... later). No visuals here.
FGBOnBuildUpChanged OnBuildUpChanged;          // (EGBElement, float Value, float Threshold)
FGBOnElementalStatusStarted OnStatusStarted;   // (EGBElement, FName Reaction, float Duration)
FGBOnElementalStatusEnded OnStatusEnded;       // (EGBElement)
FGBOnElementalStatusEnded OnImmunityEnded;     // (EGBElement)
```
Declare the delegates (native multicast) in the header.

**Config per element** (read when needed, never cached across a data reload): numbers from the owner's `UGBStatsComponent::GetStat(Key, Default)` where `Default = Data->GetGameValue(GBElemental::DefaultKey(Key), 0)` (so an enemy's `Stats` value wins, and modifiers can change it later); the reaction from the owner's enemy definition `Strings` (`AGBEnemyCharacter::GetDefinition()`), else `Data->GetGameString(DefaultKey, "None")`. Valid reactions: Fire `Ignite` / `None`; Lightning `Stun` / `Interrupt` / `None`; Ice `Freeze` / `Slow` / `None`. An unknown text logs one warning (once per enemy id and element) and counts as `None`. Reaction `None` = immune to that status: no build-up is added (the damage itself is untouched). A missing default (threshold 0) disables that bar; log one warning per key, once.

**Tick:** `PrimaryComponentTick.TickInterval = Game.json ElementalTickInterval` (set in BeginPlay; default 0.1). Tick is enabled only while some meter is not idle (enable in AddBuildUp / StartStatus, disable when all three are idle). Each tick: `Advance` each meter with DeltaTime (the engine passes the real elapsed time), broadcast `OnBuildUpChanged` on ValueChanged, and on StatusEnded / ImmunityEnded run the end logic and broadcast.

**Status start** (when `Add` returns true), with `Duration = <E>StatusDuration`, `Instigator` = the one whose hit filled the bar:
- **Fire, `Ignite`:** `UGBStatusEffectComponent::ApplyEffect("Ignite", Instigator, DurationScale = Duration / IgniteDefinition.Duration (guard against 0), StrengthScale = IgniteDamageMult)`. The Ignite effect is data in `StatusEffects.json` (ticks of fire damage through `DealDamage`, so FireDamageTaken applies and it never adds build-up).
- **Lightning:** first the discharge: if `ShockDischargeDamage > 0`, `UGBCombatLibrary::DealDamage(Owner, Info)` with that amount, Element Lightning, the instigator, `SourceId "Shock"`, `BuildUp 0`. If that killed the owner, stop here. The reaction (`Stun` / `Interrupt`) is done by the enemy through `OnStatusStarted` (below).
- **Ice, `Slow`:** `Stats->AddModifiers("Elemental.Frost", { MoveSpeed, MultiplyMin, 1 - clamp(FrostSlow, 0, 0.95) })`. `Freeze` is done by the enemy through `OnStatusStarted`.
- Then broadcast `OnStatusStarted(Element, Reaction, Duration)` (also for Ignite and Slow) and `OnBuildUpChanged` (value 0).

**Status end:** Fire: `RemoveEffect("Ignite")` (in case a data reload changed durations); Ice: `RemoveModifiers("Elemental.Frost")`; broadcast `OnStatusEnded`.

**Death and cleanup:** bind the owner's attribute `OnDeath` in BeginPlay -> `ClearAll()` (meters reset, Frost modifier removed, tick off). EndPlay: unbind and remove the Frost modifier. No timers survive the owner.

## 4. Damage path: `Combat/GBCombatLibrary.h/.cpp`
- `static int32 NewBuildUpEventId();` global counter, never returns 0.
- `static bool IsWeakPointHit(const AActor* Target, const FVector& HitLocation);` today: `AGBEnemyCharacter::IsHeadshotLocation`. The one place to add other weak points later; a head that is also a weak point is still one hit, so the bonus can never apply twice. Update the header comment.

+Modifier ops: `Add`, `Multiply`, `Override`, and `MultiplyMin` (only the lowest one on a stat counts: slows never stack, the strongest wins).

+Elemental keys (GDD 6 "Elemental build-up"): per enemy in `Enemies.json` `Stats` (`<E>DamageTaken`, `<E>BuildUpTaken`, `<E>BuildUpThreshold`, `<E>BuildUpDecayDelay`, `<E>BuildUpDecayRate`, `<E>StatusDuration`, `<E>StatusImmunity`, `IgniteDamageMult`, `ShockDischargeDamage`, `FrostSlow`; E = Fire, Lightning, Ice) and `Strings` (`<E>StatusReaction`); missing keys fall back to `Game.json` `ElementalDefault.<Key>`. ## How the main flows run

- **Cast:** input -> `UGBSpellbookComponent::TryCastSlot` (checks staff in hand, known, cooldown, mana; spends mana) -> `UGBQTEComponent::StartQTE` (slow time, sequence = power, gesture = reach; or instant when off) -> `GBSpell::ResolveCast` (data -> QTE scaling -> modifiers) -> spawn the behavior actor -> it deals damage through `UGBCombatLibrary`.
- **Shoot:** input -> `AGBGun` (fire interval, magazine, spread, recoil, pellets; every number via `GetStat`) -> hitscan -> headshot and distance falloff math in `UGBCombatLibrary` -> `DealDamage`.

- **Era travel:** `AGBPortal::Interact` -> `UGBEraSubsystem::RequestTravel` (fade out, swap era for `UGBEraComponent` actors and `_Past` / `_Future` sub-levels, teleport, restore health/mana/ammo, save checkpoint, fade in).

- **Progress:** encounters set flags in `UGBProgressSubsystem` when cleared; `UGBEraComponent` reads flags, which is how era-gated zones and past-to-future unlocks are built. Death restores the last checkpoint snapshot; flags are never rolled back (enemies do not respawn).

+- **Elemental build-up:** a hit carries `FGBDamageInfo::BuildUp` (spell param, weapon stat by element, item stat) and a `BuildUpEventId` (one per shot, cast, blast or tick). `DealDamage` passes it to the target's `UGBElementalStatusComponent` (`ApplyBuildUp`; the ice floor, which deals no damage, calls it directly), which dedupes by event id, applies the enemy's resistance and fills one of three `FGBBuildUpMeter`s. A full bar starts the status: Ignite is the `Ignite` status effect (DOT through `DealDamage`); Shock deals its discharge; Frost slow is a `MultiplyMin` modifier; stun, interrupt and freeze are done by `AGBEnemyCharacter` from the component's `OnStatusStarted` event. The component only ticks (every `ElementalTickInterval`) while a bar is not empty. Looks bind to its events; `gb.ShowElemental 1` is a debug view and `gb.BuildUp` a test command.
- **Upgrades:** `UGBSkillTreeComponent::Unlock` adds the node's modifiers to the player's stats; weapons and spells pick them up on their next read.

Smoke: `Smoke: done=True crashed=False LogGB errors=0 timedOut=False wall=69 s  log: C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\Saved\Logs\smoke_20261112-190237.log`
New SMOKE lines:
`SMOKE elemental dedupe ok=1`
`SMOKE elemental Fire triggered=1 adds=4`
`SMOKE elemental Fire ignite=1`
`SMOKE elemental Fire blockedWhileActive=1`
`SMOKE elemental Lightning triggered=1 adds=4`
`SMOKE elemental Lightning blockedWhileActive=1`
`SMOKE elemental Ice triggered=1 adds=4`
`SMOKE elemental Ice blockedWhileActive=1`
Also present as before: `SMOKE path check passed`, flamethrower `started=1`, `after=1.50s alive=0`, `interrupt alive=0`, `small hit alive=1`, `ground layers runeZ=3.0 floorZ=4.5`.

2. What changed, file by file
- `Core/GBTypes.h`: `EGBModOp::MultiplyMin` added; `FGBDamageInfo` gets `BuildUp`, `WeakPointBuildUpMult`, `BuildUpEventId`.
- `Core/GBStatNames.h`: `GBStat::BuildUp`, `GBStat::WeakPointBuildUpMult`; new `GBElemental` namespace (`ElementIndex`, `IndexToElement`, `NumElements=3`, per-element key tables built once as `static const FName[3]`, single keys `IgniteDamageMult/ShockDischargeDamage/FrostSlow`, `DefaultKey()` cached in static `TMap`, reaction names, `IgniteEffect/ShockSource/FrostSource`).
- `Stats/GBStatsComponent.h`: comment updated for `MultiplyMin`.
- `Stats/GBStatsComponent.cpp`: `AddModifiers` scales `MultiplyMin` around 1; `ApplyModifiers` keeps lowest `MultiplyMin` and multiplies with plain `Multiply`; Override unchanged.
- `Combat/GBBuildUpMeter.h/.cpp` (new, pure): `EGBBuildUpPhase`, `FGBBuildUpConfig`, `FGBBuildUpMeter::Add/Advance/IsIdle`, `EGBBuildUpEvent` mask, `FGBBuildUpEventLog::Accept` (ring of 8, biggest wins, id 0 never deduped).
- `Combat/GBElementalStatusComponent.h/.cpp` (new): `Find`, `AddBuildUp`, getters, `ClearAll`, delegates `OnBuildUpChanged/OnStatusStarted/OnStatusEnded/OnImmunityEnded`; config read live from `Stats->GetStat(Key, Data->GetGameValue(DefaultKey,0))` + enemy `Strings` else `Game.json` default; reaction validation with once-per-enemy-element warning; `None`=immune; tick interval from `Game.json`, tick only while busy; Fire Ignite via `ApplyEffect`, Lightning discharge via `DealDamage` (stop if dead), Ice Slow via `MultiplyMin`; end logic removes Ignite/Frost; death binds `OnDeath->ClearAll`, EndPlay removes Frost.
- `Combat/GBCombatLibrary.h/.cpp`: `IsWeakPointHit`, `NewBuildUpEventId` (never 0), `ApplyBuildUp`; `ApplyWeakPointBonus` now sets `bHeadshot=IsWeakPointHit` and only multiplies if `>1`; `DealDamage` calls `ApplyBuildUp` after `Dealt>0`.
- `Stats/GBAttributeComponent.cpp`: `ApplyDamage` multiplies by `<E>DamageTaken` when element is Fire/Lightning/Ice.
- `Spells/GBSpellTypes.cpp`: `MakeDamageInfo` adds `BuildUp=Get(BuildUp,0)` + new event id.
- `Spells/GBSpell_Zone.cpp`: no-damage branch creates one `MakeDamageInfo` per tick and calls `ApplyBuildUp` per target with `HitLocation=target`.
- `Weapons/GBHeldItem.cpp`: `MakeDamageInfo` after final element sets `BuildUp=GetStat(WeaponBuildUp(i),0)`, `WeakPointBuildUpMult=GetStat(...,Data->GetGameValue(...,1))`, new event id.
- `Items/GBInventoryComponent.cpp`: grenade `BuildUp=ReadItemStat(BuildUp,0)` + new event id.
- `AI/GBEnemyCharacter.h/.cpp`: `ElementalStatus` component, `GetElementalStatus`, `ControlLockTime`, `GetControlLockTime`, `InterruptAttack` (Windup->Recover), `ApplyControlLock`, `HandleElementalStatusStarted` (Stun->lock, Interrupt->interrupt, Freeze->lock), Tick pauses state timers while locked + `ResetStuck`, death clears lock, EndPlay unbinds.
- `UI/GBHUD.cpp`: `gb.ShowElemental` var, debug pass after `DrawDamageNumbers` (one `TActorIterator` only when 1, dist<4000, in front, living+present, lines for non-idle bars + `LOCK`).
- `Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`: `gb.BuildUp <Fire|Lightning|Ice> <Amount>` via `ApplyBuildUp`; smoke elemental block on TrainingDummy with dedupe/trigger/ignite/blocked checks.
- `Tests/GBElementalTests.cpp` (new): `MeterThreshold`, `MeterDecay`, `EventDedupe`.
- `Tests/GBStatsTests.cpp`: added `StrongestSlow`.
- Data: `Game.json` elemental defaults + `ElementalTickInterval` + `WeakPointBuildUpMult`; `Enemies.json` brute/future resists/thresholds/reactions; `StatusEffects.json` removed Burn/Shock/Chill, Slow->MultiplyMin, added Ignite, removed `WeaponOnHitEffect`; `Spells.json` removed OnHitEffect+EffectDuration from 6 spells, added BuildUp to 7, new descriptions; `Weapons.json` added build-ups, removed ember Burn; `Items.json` grenade BuildUp 60, removed Shock, new description.
- Comment-only: `GBSpell_Beam.h` (removed Burn example/dupe, doc BuildUp), `GBSpell_Wall.h`/`GBSpell_Orb.h`/`GBSpell_Trap.h`/`GBSpell_Projectile.h`/`GBSpell_Zone.h` doc BuildUp.

3. Call-site checks of section 5
- Projectile pierce: `AGBSpell_Projectile::StartSpell` calls `MakeDamageInfo` once into `Config.Damage`; `AGBProjectile::HitTarget` copies it per hit, same `BuildUpEventId` for whole flight; `IsValidTarget/DamagedActors` blocks second hit on same actor. Lightning bolt through 3 enemies = one build-up each, never twice. OK.
- Explosions / rune blast: fireball `Explode` copies `Config.Damage`, `DealRadialDamage` copies per target (same id); `AGBSpell_Trap::Trigger` makes one `MakeDamageInfo` then radial per target (same id). One event per blast, once per target. OK.
- Ticks: wall `DamageTick`, orb `DamageTick`, beam `DamageTick`, zone `ZoneTick` with damage all call `DamageTarget` per target, each `DamageTarget` calls `MakeDamageInfo` -> new id per target per tick. That satisfies one build-up per target per tick.
- Ice floor differs: our `ZoneTick` no-damage branch makes ONE `MakeDamageInfo` per tick shared across targets in that tick (spec literal one info per tick, `HitLocation`=target). Per-target dedupe is unaffected because logs are per-target. Noted as only call-site that shares an id across targets in one tick.
- One `MakeDamageInfo` per shot/swing/bolt: `AGBGun::PerformAttack` builds `BaseInfo` once then `FireHitscan/FireProjectile` copy per pellet/projectile (shared id, log keeps best pellet). `AGBSword::PerformAttack` builds once per swing, copies per target. `AGBStaff::PerformAttack` builds once per bolt. No per-pellet `MakeDamageInfo` found, no fix needed. Flamethrower rides `DamageTick->DamageTarget`, mana/QTE/hold/interrupt untouched.

4. Every Burn/Shock/Chill reference removed/changed
- Data: `StatusEffects.json` Burn/Shock/Chill deleted; `Spells.json` OnHitEffect Burn/Shock removed (Fireball/FireWall/Flamethrower/LightningBolt/LightningRune/StaticOrb) + EffectDuration removed where unreferenced; `Weapons.json` ember Burn removed; `Items.json` grenade Shock removed; `Game.json` no Burn/Chill/Shock effects. `grep Content/Data` for `Burn|Chill|WeaponOnHitEffect|"OnHitEffect": "Shock"` finds nothing (`ShockDischargeDamage` remains, intended).
- Code: no code still applies them. `GetActiveEnchant` still reads `WeaponOnHitEffect` but handles absent (returns None) as required; no data provides it. `MakeDamageInfo/ApplyOnHitEffect` still reads `OnHitEffect` for Slow ice floor. Test `GBSpellTests` uses Shock string in synthetic data only. Header comments updated to drop Burn/Shock examples.

5. Could not do exactly as described
- Smoke dummy: spec says find TrainingDummy by id; earlier smoke steps kill all enemies, so at 48.9s none is alive. I keep the find-first-alive logic but spawn a fresh TrainingDummy near the player if none is alive, else smoke would error. Behavior otherwise exactly as specced, ends with `ClearAll` and 1.6s before quit.
- Debug text format: spec examples `Fire 40/100`, `Lightning SHOCK Stun 0.8s`, `Ice IMMUNE 3.2s`. I draw Building as `Fire 40/100`, Active as `<Elem> <Reaction> <time>s`, Immune as `<Elem> IMMUNE <time>s`, plus `LOCK`. Same info, no game indicator.
- `FGBBuildUpEventLog` is plain C++ struct, not `USTRUCT` (UHT cannot reflect fixed C array); API matches spec.
- Tick interval clamped to >=0.01 to avoid a 0 tick; default 0.1 per spec.

6. What a person should check by playing
- Enchant gun Fire/Lightning/Ice, shoot dummy: bar fills, weak-point (head) fills 1.5x; shotgun one shot = one build-up (best pellet wins).
- Fireball 40 (25-55 QTE), wall 10/tick, flamethrower 8/0.3s tick; Ignite 4s/0.5s ticks, then 3s immune; verify no double burn.
- Lightning bolt pierce gives one stack per enemy; rune blast respects Expanded Sigil radius; orb ticks; Shock discharge + stun vs interrupt vs none per enemy (brute only interrupts).
- Ice floor alone never fills (5/0.5s over 6s=60<100) but + ice gun finishes; Frost Slow vs floor Slow strongest wins, Deep Freeze still caps 80%; Freeze locks movement/attacks then 5s immune.
- Brute thresholds higher, fire taken 0.8, brute Frost only slows; future orc lightning taken 1.25.
- `gb.ShowElemental 1` bars over heads; `gb.BuildUp Fire 30` near enemies; death clears bars/slow; lock pauses Windup/Recover timers but gravity/knockback still work.

content.content:
## Sixth block: six new perks and a flamethrower you hold
The owner sent a table of six new spell perks (one for each spell that had none, 1 point per rank, 3 ranks), then three notes on the flamethrower while the work ran: it runs while its key is held until released or out of mana; a strong hit (30% of health or more) interrupts it with a camera shake, and the description says "a strong hit" without the number; damage in fixed 0.1 s steps, not per frame (then: 0.3 s). GDD v0.20-v0.21.

| Owner's note | What was done |
|---|---|
| Six new perks (Lingering Flames, Intense Heat, Expanded Sigil, Persistent Charge, Enduring Guard, Deep Freeze). | Pure data in `Skills.json`: the modifier system already reached every spell parameter. The architect placed each in its element's column with no prerequisite, so it can be tested at once. The implementer was asked to verify in code that each perk's target parameter means what the perk says (the rune's blast is `Radius`, not the trigger radius; the floor's slow scales with `EffectStrength`) before writing the data. |
| Deep Freeze needs a limit so enemies are never stopped. | A general rule instead of a special case: any spell parameter can declare a `Cap` in `Spells.json`, applied after QTE scaling and perks. The ice floor's slow is capped at 80%. Tested. |
| (Architect's addition) | Every modifier key in the data is now checked at load: a perk pointing at a misspelled spell, parameter or weapon stat logs a warning, and the scripted run fails on warnings. Before, a typo silently did nothing. |
| Flamethrower runs while the key is held. | Data-driven beam params (`HoldToSustain`, `MinDuration`, no time limit, mana per second). A pure, tested rule decides whether the beam continues. A short minimum burn (0.75 s) keeps a cast from being wasted if the key was released during the QTE. |

input.new_string:
## Seventh block: elemental build-up (Ignite, Shock, Frost)
The owner wrote a full spec (in Spanish; verbatim in `Prompts/feedback8_elemental_spec_owner.md`): every enemy builds up fire, lightning and ice separately; a full bar starts a status (Ignite = damage over time, Shock = interruption, Frost = freeze or strong slow), with per-enemy resistances, thresholds, durations, immunity and reactions, per-spell and per-weapon build-up, a weak-point bonus, everything in data, events for future visuals, and a list of 13 checks. It ended with "if you have any questions, ask them before continuing".

The architect read the combat code first and reported the conflicts instead of building on top of them:
- Every elemental hit already applied a small effect: fire hits burned (a damage-over-time), lightning hits applied a 40% slow **already named "Shock"**, the ice enchant chilled. Adding Ignite on top would have meant two damage-over-time systems and two meanings of "Shock".
- Slows multiplied (ice floor 50% x chill 30% = 65%), against the spec's "Frost must not stack uncontrollably with the ice floor".
- There were no elemental resistances at all, only a general damage-taken multiplier.
- In this game the weapon enchant works on guns only; the elemental sword and the ember staff have elements of their own.

It asked two design questions (and decided every engineering question itself, as the owner asked). Translated from Spanish:
1. "What do we do with the existing per-hit effects?" Owner: **remove them all**; the bar's status is the only elemental effect (the ice floor keeps its zone slow).
2. "Should the elemental sword and the ember staff build up too?" Owner: **yes, both**.

| Part of the spec | How it was built |
|---|---|
| Three independent bars per enemy, threshold, decay after a delay, reset on trigger, no build-up while active, immunity after | A pure, tested struct (`FGBBuildUpMeter`) with three phases (building, active, immune). Decay is computed from elapsed time, so one 1 s step equals ten 0.1 s steps (tested). One small component per enemy (`UGBElementalStatusComponent`) holds three meters and only ticks while a bar is not empty, 10 times a second: an idle horde costs nothing. |
| No duplicate build-up from one hit, explosions, piercing shots, shotguns | Every hit carries an event id: one per shot, cast, blast or tick. Each enemy remembers its last 8 ids, and a repeated id only adds the part above what it already added. The eight pellets of a shotgun shot give one build-up, and the best pellet counts (a head pellet after a body pellet adds only the difference). Tested. |
| Reuse the existing damage events | Build-up rides on the one damage function (`DealDamage`). The flamethrower's 0.3 s ticks, the fire wall's and the orb's ticks, the rune's blast and the fireball's explosion needed no change at all. Only the ice floor, which deals no damage, sends its build-up directly from its existing tick. |
| Per-enemy configuration, damage and build-up resistances separate, defaults only as fallback | Plain enemy stats in `Enemies.json` (`FireDamageTaken`, `FireBuildUpTaken`, `FireBuildUpThreshold`, `LightningStatusReaction`...), read through the existing stat system, so perks can modify them later. A value an enemy does not set falls back to `Game.json` `ElementalDefault.*`. The brute only gets interrupted by Shock and only slowed by Frost; the armored orc is weak to lightning. |
| Ignite must not duplicate Fireball's burn | The burn is gone (owner's answer). Ignite reuses the existing status effect system for its damage ticks, so there is one damage-over-time system. |
| Shock: discharge, interrupt, stun, or immune; Frost: freeze or strong slow | A Shock discharge is a small hit of lightning damage. Stun and freeze pause the enemy's state machine (its attack timers stop too); interrupt cancels only the attack being wound up. The reaction is an enemy string; "None" makes it immune to the status but not to the damage. |
| Frost and ice floor slows must not stack | A new modifier operation, `MultiplyMin`: among those on a stat, only the strongest counts. The ice floor's 50%, Deep Freeze's 55/60/65% and its 80% cap are unchanged (tested). |
| Weak-point bonus once, without touching the head damage bonus | The weak-point check was split out of the damage bonus (`IsWeakPointHit`), the single place to add non-head weak points later. A hit is either on a weak point or not, so the bonus cannot apply twice. |
| Events for visuals, no universal indicator | The component broadcasts "build-up changed", "status started" and "status ended" for each enemy's future look. For testing only: `gb.ShowElemental 1` prints the bars over enemies, and `gb.BuildUp Fire 30` adds build-up to nearby enemies. |

- **Who did what:** the architect wrote the design (`Prompts/feedback8_elemental_buildup.md`: types, rules, data keys and values, tests, smoke checks); one Muse Spark batch implemented it (28 files, 4 new). Its builds, 34 tests (4 new) and the scripted run passed on the first try. The scripted run now fills each bar on a training dummy, checks that Ignite runs, that a full bar refuses more build-up while active, and that a repeated event counts once.
- **Where the AI failed in this block:** splitting the weak-point check from the damage bonus (asked for in the brief) had a side effect neither the brief nor Muse saw: spell projectiles, which have no head bonus, started flagging head hits as headshots, which shows them as "big" damage numbers. The architect found it reading the diff and made projectiles look for the weak point only when the shot has a head bonus. The brief's own example was also slightly wrong: Muse noticed that the scripted run kills every enemy before the elemental step, and spawns a fresh training dummy instead of failing.

## Design decisions
All taken by the architect;

lines: # Handoff between architect chats
-> Kept by whichever Claude Code chat is the architect. Read `CLAUDE.md`, `Design/GDD.md` (v0.21) and `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` first; this file says where things stand and how the work is run.

-> Last update: 2026-11-12 (day 1, sixth block: six new spell perks, hold-to-sustain flamethrower with strong-hit interrupt), by the second architect chat (Claude Opus 5.5), which took over from the first one (Claude Fable 5.2).
+> Kept by whichever Claude Code chat is the architect. Read `CLAUDE.md`, `Design/GDD.md` (v0.22) and `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` first; this file says where things stand and how the work is run.

+> Last update: 2026-11-12 (day 1, seventh block: elemental build-up with Ignite, Shock and Frost), by the second architect chat (Claude Opus 5.5), which took over from the first one (Claude Fable 5.2).
## Standing instructions from the owner (2026-11-12)
- Do not stop to ask for go-aheads or yes/no questions. Decide, do, log. If the architect stops, the project stops.
| QTE time, keys, gestures | `QTE.json`; `QTE/GBQTELogic.cpp`, `QTE/GBQTEComponent.cpp` |
| Enemies: health, damage, ranges, speed, drops | `Enemies.json`, `Encounters.json`; movement tuning (`Enemy*` keys) in `Game.json`; `AI/GBEnemyCharacter.cpp` |
| Perks (and the reset: `ResetAll`) | `Skills.json` (modifier keys: `Weapon.<Id|Gun|Staff|Sword|All>.<Stat>`, `Spell.<Id|All>.<Param>`, player stats by name) |
-| Burn, chill, shock, slows | `StatusEffects.json` |
+| Slows, Ignite's damage ticks, potions, enchant buffs | `StatusEffects.json` |

+| Elemental build-up: per-enemy thresholds, resistances, reactions, durations | `Enemies.json` (per enemy), `Game.json` `ElementalDefault.*` (fallbacks); spell `BuildUp` param; weapon `FireBuildUp` / `LightningBuildUp` / `IceBuildUp`; code `Combat/GBElementalStatusComponent.cpp`, `Combat/GBBuildUpMeter.cpp` |
| Items, armor, recipes | `Items.json`; `Items/GBInventoryComponent.cpp` |
| HUD, menus, damage numbers | `UI/GBHUD*.cpp`; damage-number tuning in `Game.json` |
| Kill height, corpse time, global values | `Game.json` |

`powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools\Devlog\Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1 -Agent codex -Model 'gpt-6.1-sol (medium)' -PromptFile Prompts\X.md -Purpose '...' -Shell cmd -Command 'codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=medium -s read-only -C . - < Prompts\X.md'`
A data-only change (JSON) needs no build: run the tests and the smoke script, then package.
-## Right now (end of the sixth block, 2026-11-12)
+## Right now (end of the seventh block, 2026-11-12)

+- **Seventh block (GDD v0.22, owner's spec `Prompts/feedback8_elemental_spec_owner.md`):** elemental build-up on every enemy (three bars, Ignite / Shock / Frost, per-enemy resistances and reactions, spell and weapon build-up, one count per event, weak-point bonus, `MultiplyMin` slows). The old per-hit Burn / Shock slow / Chill were removed (owner's answer). Debug: `gb.ShowElemental 1`, `gb.BuildUp <Element> <Amount>`. 34 tests; smoke fills each bar on a training dummy. Not played yet. Not reviewed by Codex (one Muse batch, read by the architect; one fix: spell projectiles no longer flag head hits as headshots).
- Everything is committed on `main` (last commits: perks and flamethrower, beam interrupt, then the seventh package's docs), and pushed to GitHub (`VDuk3/EpicAIMegaJam`).

- Editor build and game build green; 30 pure-logic tests pass; the smoke run (now with a skill reset check and a ground-spell screenshot, `10_ground_spells`) ends with no errors, also on the packaged exe. Package: `Glyphbound/TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`, 245.4 MB.
- Six blocks done today:
7. End of day (if not done again after the last block): package, `New-DevlogDay.ps1`, commit. On Nov 13 start a new day entry `Devlog/days/2026-11-13.md` from `Devlog/TEMPLATE_DAY.md`.
## Things a human must check by playing

+- Build 8 (elemental): with `gb.ShowElemental 1`: fire spells fill the fire bar and Ignite burns 4 s then 3 s immune; a lightning bolt through a line of orcs gives each one build-up; a full lightning bar stuns an orc (stops, attack cancelled) but only interrupts the brute; the ice floor alone fills slowly and decays, an ice-enchanted gun finishes it; frozen orcs stop, the brute only slows; Frost on the ice floor does not slow more than the strongest of the two; a shotgun shot counts once; head shots fill faster; the flamethrower and the ice floor (Deep Freeze) feel the same as before.

- Build 7: the six new perks (each at rank 3), the flamethrower held / released / out of mana, a strong hit interrupting it (shake, message, aim unchanged), a small hit not interrupting it, with the ice shield raised the blocked part not counting.
- Build 6: overlapping rune and ice floor in both orders (the last one fully on top, no flicker, also while moving).
- Build 5: the rune and ice floor figures (full area, flat, sharp, floor visible through them, rune dim until armed), the +1 skill point button.

lines: | Weak-point bonus once, without touching the head damage bonus | The weak-point check was split out of the damage bonus (`IsWeakPointHit`), the single place to add non-head weak points later. A hit is either on a weak point or not, so the bonus cannot apply twice. |

| Events for visuals, no universal indicator | The component broadcasts "build-up changed", "status started" and "status ended" for each enemy's future look. For testing only: `gb.ShowElemental 1` prints the bars over enemies, and `gb.BuildUp Fire 30` adds build-up to nearby enemies. |
+- **Result:** eighth package, `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip` 245.4 MB; the packaged exe passes the scripted run with the new elemental checks. Not played by a person yet.

- **Who did what:** the architect wrote the design (`Prompts/feedback8_elemental_buildup.md`: types, rules, data keys and values, tests, smoke checks); one Muse Spark batch implemented it (28 files, 4 new). Its builds, 34 tests (4 new) and the scripted run passed on the first try. The scripted run now fills each bar on a training dummy, checks that Ignite runs, that a full bar refuses more build-up while active, and that a repeated event counts once.

- **Where the AI failed in this block:** splitting the weak-point check from the damage bonus (asked for in the brief) had a side effect neither the brief nor Muse saw: spell projectiles, which have no head bonus, started flagging head hits as headshots, which shows them as "big" damage numbers. The architect found it reading the diff and made projectiles look for the weak point only when the shot has a head bonus. The brief also assumed the training dummy would still be alive at the end of the scripted run; Muse found that earlier steps remove every enemy, and spawns a fresh dummy for the elemental step instead of failing.
