content.text:
El sistema de acumulación elemental está hecho y empaquetado, pero nadie lo ha jugado todavía, así que los valores son provisionales. Para probarlo, descomprime de nuevo `Glyphbound/TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`.

**Verificación**
- Las dos compilaciones (Editor y juego) salen bien.
- Pasan los 34 tests (4 nuevos).
- El recorrido automático pasa sin errores en el Editor y en el exe empaquetado. En un muñeco de práctica llena cada barra, comprueba que Ignite quema, que una barra activa no acepta más acumulación y que un mismo impacto cuenta una sola vez.

**Tus respuestas, aplicadas**
- Quité los efectos pequeños por golpe: la quemadura del fuego, el 40 % de ralentización del rayo y el Chill del hielo. El estado al llenar la barra es el único efecto elemental. El Ice Floor conserva su ralentización de zona, con Deep Freeze y el tope del 80 % sin cambios.
- La espada elemental y el bastón Ember también acumulan su elemento.
- La granada eléctrica acumula rayo, porque el "Shock" que aplicaba ya no existe (decisión mía).

**Cómo funciona**
- **Una barra por elemento en cada enemigo.** Se llena con los impactos, empieza a bajar si pasan 2 s sin acumular y, al llenarse, vuelve a cero y activa el estado. Después hay un tiempo de inmunidad.
- **Sin acumulación duplicada.** La escopeta cuenta una vez por disparo y cuenta el mejor perdigón. Lightning Bolt da una acumulación a cada enemigo que atraviesa.
- **Reutiliza los eventos de daño que ya había.** El lanzallamas acumula en sus mismos ticks de 0,3 s; el maná, el QTE, la canalización y la interrupción no cambian.
- **Cada enemigo con su configuración.** El orco bruto solo se interrumpe con Shock y solo se ralentiza con Frost, y sus umbrales son más altos. El orco del futuro es débil al rayo.
- **Ralentizaciones:** si coinciden la del Ice Floor y la de Frost, solo cuenta la más fuerte.
- **Cabeza o punto débil:** multiplica la acumulación ×1,5, sin tocar el bonus de daño por headshot.
- **Para los efectos visuales:** cada enemigo emite eventos de acumulación, inicio y fin del estado. Todavía no hay ningún indicador visual en el juego.

**Una corrección mía:** al revisar el código vi que los proyectiles de hechizo marcaban los golpes en la cabeza como headshot y salían con número de daño grande. Lo arreglé.

**Para probar**, en la consola:
- `gb.ShowElemental 1` muestra las barras encima de los enemigos (solo para pruebas).
- `gb.BuildUp Fire 30` añade acumulación a los enemigos cercanos.

**Qué mirar jugando**
- Ignite: 4 s quemando y luego 3 s de inmunidad.
- El aturdimiento del orco frente a la interrupción del bruto.
- El Ice Floor solo no completa la barra (como mucho llega a 60 de 100) y un arma encantada con hielo la termina.
- Un orco congelado se queda quieto, sin atacar.
- Que el lanzallamas y el Ice Floor se sientan igual que antes.

Todos los valores están en los JSON. Las decisiones están en el GDD v0.22 (sección "Elemental build-up") y en la [entrada del día](Devlog/days/2026-11-12.md).

# Code review: Glyphbound, changes after the owner's first play-test (read-only)

You are the second-opinion reviewer for **Glyphbound**, a first-person RPG shooter in Unreal Engine 5.9.0 (C++), made for a 4-day game jam. Do not modify any file. Do not build or run anything.

## Context
- Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` first (short). The design is in `Design/GDD.md`; the changelog entry v0.14 at the top lists what the owner asked for after playing the first build.
- The change under review is everything between git commit `798a4e5` and `HEAD` (`git diff 798a4e5 HEAD --stat`, then read the files). It was written by four AI implementers in parallel (reports in `Prompts/feedback1_notes.md`) and then compiled and integrated by a fifth. It builds, the tests pass and a scripted smoke run passes, so a missing include is NOT what we want from you.
- Code: `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/`. Data: `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json`.
- Engine source for checking APIs: `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9\Engine\Source`.

## What changed (review these areas)
1. **Owned weapons** (`Weapons/GBEquipmentComponent.*`, `World/GBPickup.*`, `World/GBChest.cpp`, `Items/GBInventoryComponent.cpp`, `World/GBProgressSubsystem.h`): a picked-up weapon joins the owned list and goes to the hands only if its slot is empty; the player equips owned weapons from the Weapons page of the inventory. Ammo and element of stored weapons must survive swaps, checkpoints, death and era travel.
2. **Held ice shield** (`Spells/GBSpell_Shield.*`, `Spells/GBSpellbookComponent.*`, `Player/GBPlayerCharacter.*`, `Player/GBInputSet.*`): the spell summons a shield for a duration; the Block input (Q / L2, hold) raises it; only a raised shield blocks, and only from the front. Look for: the shield blocking when lowered, never expiring, surviving death or era travel wrongly, the move-speed modifier left on after it ends, blocking while a menu is open, the L2 conflict with the spell modifier on gamepad.
3. **Mouse in menus** (`Player/GBPlayerController.*`, `UI/GBHUD*.cpp`): cursor shown in menus, click handling through hit rects, input mode switched on open / close. Look for: the cursor or the UI input mode left on after closing a menu or after death / respawn, a click acting twice, clicks acting on a stale hit rect of a previous frame or menu, the game staying paused.
4. **Kill-Z** (`Core/GBGameMode.*`, `Player/GBPlayerCharacter.*`, `AI/GBEnemyCharacter.*`): falling below `KillZ` kills the player (once) and enemies (through the attribute component so encounters progress).
5. **Damage numbers** (`UI/GBHUD_DamageNumbers.cpp`, `Combat/GBCombatLibrary.*` global event): look for delegate lifetime problems (HUD destroyed and still bound, bound twice after a respawn), unbounded growth, numbers for the player's own damage taken.
6. **Explosions and textured structures** (`Combat/GBExplosionEffect.*`, `Combat/GBProjectile.*`, `Spells/GBSpell_Projectile.*`, `Spells/GBSpell_Wall.*`, `Core/GBPlaceholder.cpp`, `UI/GBPixelSpriteLibrary.*`, `Tools/Jam/make_materials.py`): every projectile explosion path must spawn the shockwave exactly once and never damage twice; knockback only on hostile characters; the material `/Game/Glyphbound/Materials/M_PixelSurface` must load in a packaged build (see `Glyphbound/Config/DefaultGame.ini`) and missing-material fallbacks must not crash.
7. **Enemy pathing** (`AI/GBSteering.*`, `AI/GBEnemyCharacter.*`, `World/GBTestArena.*`, `Config/DefaultEngine.ini`): navmesh built at runtime plus a local steering fallback and a stuck check. Look for: state machine dead ends (an enemy that can never attack because of the new line-of-sight rule, e.g. the trace hitting its own capsule, the player's shield, another enemy or an era-hidden prop), steering toward ledges, timers never reset, enemies frozen after era travel.

## What to report (real defects only, most severe first)
- Runtime bugs a player would hit, state that leaks between death / respawn / era travel / menus, and contract breaks between the modules above.
- Data and code mismatches: a key in a JSON file that the code spells differently or never reads, and the reverse.
- Things that work in the Editor but break in a packaged build.
- Real balance numbers hardcoded where data should decide.

Do not report: style, naming, formatting, missing comments, micro-optimizations, multiplayer issues (single player), or the number of tests.

## Output format
A numbered list, most severe first, at most 20 items. For each:
- `file:line` (or lines),
- what is wrong, in one or two sentences,
- why it matters when playing (what the player would see),
- the smallest fix you would make.
Finish with one short paragraph: the three things you would fix first, and anything you checked and found solid.

# Code review: Glyphbound, elemental build-up (read-only)

You are the second-opinion reviewer for **Glyphbound**, a first-person RPG shooter in Unreal Engine 5.9.0 (C++), made for a 4-day game jam. Do not modify any file. Do not build or run anything.

## Context
- Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` first (short). The design is `Design/GDD.md` section 6 "Elemental build-up" (v0.22) and the v0.22 lines of section 18 "Numbers". The owner's original spec (Spanish) is `Prompts/feedback8_elemental_spec_owner.md`; the architect's design brief given to the implementer is `Prompts/feedback8_elemental_buildup.md`.
- The change under review is commit `99ee8f8` (`git show 99ee8f8 --stat`, then read the files). One AI implementer wrote it; the architect added one fix in `Combat/GBProjectile.cpp`. It builds, 34 tests pass, and a scripted smoke run passes in the Editor and in the packaged exe, so a missing include is NOT what we want from you.
- Code: `Glyphbound/Source/Glyphbound/`. Data: `Glyphbound/Content/Data/*.json`.
- Engine source for checking APIs: `C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9\Engine\Source`.

## What changed (review these areas)
1. **Meters** (`Combat/GBBuildUpMeter.*`): three phases (building, active, immune), decay after a delay, frame-rate independence, the event log that makes one event count once (biggest amount wins).
2. **Component** (`Combat/GBElementalStatusComponent.*`): config read from enemy stats with `Game.json` `ElementalDefault.*` fallbacks, reactions from enemy strings, tick only while busy (`SetComponentTickEnabled`, `TickInterval`), Ignite through `UGBStatusEffectComponent`, Shock discharge through `DealDamage` (re-entrancy: it damages its own owner from inside a damage call chain), Frost slow as a `MultiplyMin` modifier, cleanup on death / EndPlay / data reload.
3. **Damage path** (`Combat/GBCombatLibrary.*`, `Stats/GBAttributeComponent.cpp`, `Core/GBTypes.h`, `Core/GBStatNames.h`): `ApplyBuildUp` after a damaging hit, `IsWeakPointHit` split from `ApplyWeakPointBonus`, per-element damage taken, event ids.
4. **Sources** (`Spells/GBSpellTypes.cpp`, `Spells/GBSpell_Zone.cpp`, `Weapons/GBHeldItem.cpp`, `Items/GBInventoryComponent.cpp`, `Combat/GBProjectile.cpp`): one event id per shot / cast / blast / tick; shotgun pellets, piercing bolts, the fireball explosion, the rune blast (`Spells/GBSpell_Trap.cpp`), the flamethrower ticks (`Spells/GBSpell_Beam.cpp`), the ice floor (no damage, so it sends build-up directly).
5. **Enemy reactions** (`AI/GBEnemyCharacter.*`): stun / freeze lock that pauses the state machine, interrupt that cancels a windup. Look for: an enemy stuck forever, an attack landing after it was cancelled (a melee hit or a ranged projectile scheduled by a timer), movement continuing while locked, locks surviving death or era travel.
6. **Stats** (`Stats/GBStatsComponent.*`): the new `MultiplyMin` op; the ice floor's `Slow` effect now uses it; Deep Freeze and the 80% cap must be unchanged.
7. **Removed per-hit effects** (`Burn`, the old `Shock` slow, `Chill`): anything in code or data that still refers to them, or code that silently depended on them.
8. **Debug view and commands** (`UI/GBHUD.cpp` `gb.ShowElemental`, `Core/GBDevCommands.cpp` `gb.BuildUp` and the smoke step).

## What to report (real defects only, most severe first)
- Runtime bugs a player would hit: wrong build-up amounts (double counting, never counting), statuses that never end or never start, immunity not respected, slows stacking, Ignite damage that differs from the data, crashes on death / destroy / data reload.
- Contract breaks with existing systems: the flamethrower (mana, hold, interrupt), the ice floor (slow, Deep Freeze, QTE), weapon damage and head bonus, encounter progress on death.
- Data and code mismatches: a key in a JSON file that the code spells differently or never reads, and the reverse.
- Things that work in the Editor but break in a packaged build.
- Per-frame costs that grow with the number of enemies (the game will have hordes).
- Gameplay numbers hardcoded where data should decide.

Do not report: style, naming, formatting, missing comments, micro-optimizations, multiplayer issues (single player), or the number of tests.

## Output format
A numbered list, most severe first, at most 15 items. For each:
- `file:line` (or lines),
- what is wrong, in one or two sentences,
- why it matters when playing (what the player would see),
- the smallest fix you would make.
Finish with one short paragraph: the three things you would fix first, and anything you checked and found solid.

2. **Component** (`Combat/GBElementalStatusComponent.*`): config read from enemy stats with `Game.json` `ElementalDefault.*` fallbacks, reactions from enemy strings, tick only while busy (`SetComponentTickEnabled`, `TickInterval`), Ignite through `UGBStatusEffectComponent`, Shock discharge through `DealDamage` (re-entrancy: it damages its own owner from inside a damage call chain), Frost slow as a `MultiplyMin` modifier, cleanup on death / EndPlay / data reload.
3. **Damage path** (`Combat/GBCombatLibrary.*`, `Stats/GBAttributeComponent.cpp`, `Core/GBTypes.h`, `Core/GBStatNames.h`): `ApplyBuildUp` after a damaging hit, `IsWeakPointHit` split from `ApplyWeakPointBonus`, per-element damage taken, event ids.
4. **Sources** (`Spells/GBSpellTypes.cpp`, `Spells/GBSpell_Zone.cpp`, `Weapons/GBHeldItem.cpp`, `Items/GBInventoryComponent.cpp`, `Combat/GBProjectile.cpp`): one event id per shot / cast / blast / tick; shotgun pellets, piercing bolts, the fireball explosion, the rune blast (`Spells/GBSpell_Trap.cpp`), the flamethrower ticks (`Spells/GBSpell_Beam.cpp`), the ice floor (no damage, so it sends build-up directly).
5. **Enemy reactions** (`AI/GBEnemyCharacter.*`): stun / freeze lock that pauses the state machine, interrupt that cancels a windup. Look for: an enemy stuck forever, an attack landing after it was cancelled (a melee hit or a ranged projectile scheduled by a timer), movement continuing while locked, locks surviving death or era travel.
6. **Stats** (`Stats/GBStatsComponent.*`): the new `MultiplyMin` op; the ice floor's `Slow` effect now uses it; Deep Freeze and the 80% cap must be unchanged.
7. **Removed per-hit effects** (`Burn`, the old `Shock` slow, `Chill`): anything in code or data that still refers to them, or code that silently depended on them.
8. **Debug view and commands** (`UI/GBHUD.cpp` `gb.ShowElemental`, `Core/GBDevCommands.cpp` `gb.BuildUp` and the smoke step).

## What to report (real defects only, most severe first)
- Runtime bugs a player would hit: wrong build-up amounts (double counting, never counting), statuses that never end or never start, immunity not respected, slows stacking, Ignite damage that differs from the data, crashes on death / destroy / data reload.
- Contract breaks with existing systems: the flamethrower (mana, hold, interrupt), the ice floor (slow, Deep Freeze, QTE), weapon damage and head bonus, encounter progress on death.
- Data and code mismatches: a key in a JSON file that the code spells differently or never reads, and the reverse.
- Things that work in the Editor but break in a packaged build.
- Per-frame costs that grow with the number of enemies (the game will have hordes).
- Gameplay numbers hardcoded where data should decide.

Do not report: style, naming, formatting, missing comments, micro-optimizations, multiplayer issues (single player), or the number of tests.

## Output format
A numbered list, most severe first, at most 15 items. For each:
- `file:line` (or lines),
- what is wrong, in one or two sentences,
- why it matters when playing (what the player would see),
- the smallest fix you would make.
Finish with one short paragraph: the three things you would fix first, and anything you checked and found solid.

lines: - **Result:** eighth package, `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip` 245.4 MB; the packaged exe passes the scripted run with the new elemental checks. Not played by a person yet.

- **Who did what:** the architect wrote the design (`Prompts/feedback8_elemental_buildup.md`: types, rules, data keys and values, tests, smoke checks); one Muse Spark batch implemented it (28 files, 4 new). Its builds, 34 tests (4 new) and the scripted run passed on the first try. The scripted run now fills each bar on a training dummy, checks that Ignite runs, that a full bar refuses more build-up while active, and that a repeated event counts once.

- **Where the AI failed in this block:** splitting the weak-point check from the damage bonus (asked for in the brief) had a side effect neither the brief nor Muse saw: spell projectiles, which have no head bonus, started flagging head hits as headshots, which shows them as "big" damage numbers. The architect found it reading the diff and made projectiles look for the weak point only when the shot has a head bonus. The brief also assumed the training dummy would still be alive at the end of the scripted run; Muse found that earlier steps remove every enemy, and spawns a fresh dummy for the elemental step instead of failing.

+- **Review (the owner asked for it after the package):** Codex CLI with GPT Sol 6.1 at medium, read-only (`Prompts/feedback8_review_codex.md`), found three real defects, all small, and called the shotgun dedupe, piercing and blast delivery, Shock killing its own target, windup cancellation, era pause, strongest-slow and the Deep Freeze cap solid:

+  1. Ignite could lose its last damage tick (7 ticks instead of 8): the meters were advanced by the whole tick interval even when the status had started in the middle of it, and the meter's end removed the Ignite effect early. Fix: the component keeps its own clock and gives back the time between the last tick and the hit; Ignite now runs out on its own.
+  2. The `ElementalDefault.<E>DamageTaken` values in `Game.json` were never read (the code fell back to 1). Fix: they are now the fallback for enemies that set no value.
+  3. A long frame (a hitch) that ran past both the status and the immunity left the bar immune for one extra tick. Fix: both end in the same step; a test case covers it.

+  The architect made the three fixes directly instead of through Muse Spark (an exception to the implementer rule): about 60 lines in four files, smaller than the brief that would have described them.
## Design decisions

All taken by the architect; the owner asked not to be consulted on engineering. The provisional gameplay rules and numbers that had to be invented are listed in GDD section 18 for the owner to confirm or change.

lines: 1. Ignite could lose its last damage tick (7 ticks instead of 8): the meters were advanced by the whole tick interval even when the status had started in the middle of it, and the meter's end removed the Ignite effect early. Fix: the component keeps its own clock and gives back the time between the last tick and the hit; Ignite now runs out on its own.
2. The `ElementalDefault.<E>DamageTaken` values in `Game.json` were never read (the code fell back to 1). Fix: they are now the fallback for enemies that set no value.
3. A long frame (a hitch) that ran past both the status and the immunity left the bar immune for one extra tick. Fix: both end in the same step; a test case covers it.

Codex (Sol 6.1, medium, solo lectura) encontró 3 defectos pequeños en el sistema elemental. Ya están corregidos y hay un paquete nuevo, pero nadie lo ha jugado todavía.

**Lo que encontró y cómo quedó:**
1. **Ignite podía perder su último tick de daño** (7 ticks en vez de 8: 42 de daño en vez de 48). Ahora el componente lleva su propio reloj: el estado empieza en el momento del impacto, no en el tick anterior. Además, Ignite ya no se corta a mano y dura exactamente lo que dicen los datos.
2. **Los valores `ElementalDefault.*DamageTaken` de `Game.json` no se leían**: el código usaba siempre 1. Ahora son el valor de respaldo para los enemigos que no definen el suyo.
